PARK CANNON.name: Park Cannon
PARK CANNON.background: Ran as a Democrat in the partisan races on record. Won the race for State House District 58 in 2016, 2018 (unopposed), 2020 (unopposed), 2022 (unopposed) and 2024 (unopposed). Served in the Georgia General Assembly: House District 58 (2015-2016, 2017-2018, 2019-2020, 2021-2022, 2023-2024, 2025-2026).

positions.stance: Would advocate for balanced, smart and neighborhood-approved neighborhood growth, would be a voice for affordable housing in the City of Atlanta, prioritizes increasing affordable housing units in communities and secured state tax relief for supportive housing.
q: As your State Representative, I will continue to advocate for growth in our neighborhoods to be balanced, smart and neighborhood-approved.
I sit on the City of Atlanta Delegation as Co-chair of the Affordable Housing Sub-Committee to be a voice for all of us to move forward with the city and not be left behind.

positions.stance: Would increase affordable healthcare for all, supports protecting and increasing access to quality affordable healthcare and expanded postpartum Medicaid, focused on fibroids and provided cash flow services to families.
q: I will work to increase affordable healthcare for all, not just for some.
She knows that it is imperative that we protect and increase access to quality affordable healthcare.

positions.stance: Supports ensuring voters have access to the ballot and their votes counted, was unlawfully arrested for protecting voting rights, charges later dropped.
q: Now that the charges have been dropped, I continue forward as a staunch supporter of all Georgia voters to ensure they they have access to the ballot, their votes counted, and to be able to pick their elected officials— not the other way around.
Park was unlawfully arrested in March of 2021 upon knocking on the Governor’s door to protect voting rights and her charges were dropped as the world watched in shock.

positions.stance: Voted for public awareness campaign for crypto, web3 and blockchain education and pushing for comprehensive sexual education, supports ensuring rights of pregnant people and providing access to education.
q: We just voted for the public awareness campaign for crypto, web3 and blockchain education and are pushing for comprehensive sexual education.
From ensuring the rights of pregnant people are represented and protected to providing access to education, when HD 58 needs aid Park is there.

positions.stance: Would bring more good jobs to families.
q: I will work every day to bring more good jobs to our families.

positions.stance: Secured state tax relief for supportive housing on Murphy Avenue.
q: We just secured state tax relief for supportive housing on Murphy Avenue.

positions.stance: Introduces Six Penny Plan to balance federal budget in five years; says interest payments on debt exceed spending on national defense, crowding out core priorities; says a spending freeze was enough to balance the budget within five years in 2018.
q: Dr. Rand Paul Introduces Six Penny Plan to Balance the Federal Budget in Five Years
Interest payments on the debt now exceed what America spends on national defense, a sign of how borrowing is crowding out core priorities.

positions.stance: Says legislation streamlines biosimilar approval by eliminating clinical study requirements; supports legislation to lower drug prices and increase access to treatments; would eliminate FDA's requirement for pharmacodynamics and clinical efficacy studies.
q: Washington, D.C. – Yesterday, the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee unanimously advanced legislation introduced by U.S. Senator Rand Paul (R-KY) to streamline the approval process for biosimilars by eliminating costly and redundant clinical study requirements.
Dr. Paul’s Expedited Access to Biosimilars Act will increase market competition, lower drug prices, and increase access to more life-saving treatments.

positions.stance: Opposes 100 percent tariff on China, would reject bill that raises prices and weakens dollar, and says legislation aims to punish Vladimir Putin.
q: Slapping a 100 percent tariff on China may inadvertently solidify its geopolitical alignment with Russia as Beijing would become more, not less, reliant on Moscow for economic and diplomatic support.

If not adopted, Congress should reject this strategic blunder of a bill that will do nothing to bring peace to Ukraine, but rather raise prices for American consumers, further weaken the dollar, destroy U.S. relations around the globe, and drive our adversaries closer together.”

positions.stance: Would strip counterproductive tariffs from legislation and says taxation bills must originate in the House of Representatives.
q: I encourage my colleagues to support my amendment that strips the counterproductive tariffs from the legislation.
Moreover, taxation bills must originate in the House of Representatives.

positions.stance: Supports checking Trump’s abuse of authority and assault on freedoms; says authored court reform bills including ethics code, term limits, and court expansion; supports requiring judges to place financial assets into blind trusts.
q: We can put a check on Trump’s abuse of his authority and his assault on our freedom and liberties.

Congressman Johnson is the author of several court reform bills, including requiring SCOTUS justices to adhere to a binding code of ethics, setting term limits for justices at 18 years and expanding the court from nine to 13 justices.

positions.stance: Says led letter to EPA to reinstate funding for Solar for All program; says Georgia families have higher energy bills and fewer job opportunities; says urges office to approach matter with transparency and urgency for resilient energy grid, reduced costs, and economic opportunities.
q: WASHINGTON, D.C. – This week, Congressman Hank Johnson (GA-04) led a Georgia delegation letter to Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin pressing him to reinstate funding for the Solar for All program that invested $7 billion in clean-energy grants to 60 state, tribal, municipal, a
This leaves Georgia families with higher energy bills and fewer job opportunities, while utilities struggle to meet the growing demand for power.

positions.stance: Says economy is rigged against working people under Trump; would end Trump’s tariffs and endless war to protect economy.
q: Under Trump, we can see just how much this economy is rigged against the working people of this country.

If we do what we need to do over these next three weeks, we can begin the process of ending Trump’s endless war, and ending Trump’s tariffs, both of which wrecked the economy and caused the price of groceries and gas to go through the roof.

positions.stance: Says Trump terminated collective bargaining agreements and banned union activities; says union challenged Trump’s unconstitutional executive orders.
q: Soon after returning to the White House Trump signed an executive order terminating collective bargaining agreements negotiated by NTEU, and to kill the union they banned automatic dues deduction and banned employees from displaying NTEU labeled paraphernalia from workplaces and workspaces.
Under the leadership of NTEU national president Doreen Greenwald, the union has aggressively punched back, filing federal lawsuits, challenging Trump’s unconstitutional executive orders.

positions.stance: Supports protecting right to vote and voting process integrity; supports restoring Voting Rights Act and reforming Supreme Court.
q: So, we must remain vigilant to protect the precious right to vote, and the integrity of the voting process.

The resolution calls for the House to adopt legislation to restore and strengthen the Voting Rights Act of 1965 and – when Democrats retake the majority in the House – the elimination of the 60-vote threshold in the Senate and enactment of fundamental reforms to the Supreme Court.

positions.stance: Supports legislative package to restore faith in judiciary and address abuses of power; says worked on police and court reform, consumer protection, civil and voting rights, First Amendment rights, environmental protection, and renewable energy.
q: In the wake of an unprecedented Supreme Court term defined by historic rollbacks of the Voting Rights Act and other democratic guardrails, Johnson is supporting a legislative package that includes bills to restore faith in the federal judiciary and address abuses of power, including by Supreme Court
He is nationally known for his work on police and court reform, consumer protection, civil and voting rights, First Amendment rights, environmental protection, and renewable energy.

positions.stance: Says funding trains law enforcement, judges, and public defenders to respond to teen trauma; supports funding for water infrastructure, public safety, parks, and economic vitality.

positions.stance: Supports improving transit infrastructure and enhancing system safety; says realignment of Chestnut Drive is a transformative safety priority.

positions.stance: Supports voting to protect natural resources and address climate change.
q: Voting to protect our natural resources and the planet from existential climate change isn’t difficult, it’s just common sense.

positions.stance: Says funding brings vision for Ashford Forest Preserve to ensure accessibility.

positions.stance: Prioritizes cutting taxes, creating jobs, supporting law enforcement, and expanding school choice, worked with Governor Kemp to author legislation that reins in lawsuit abuse and protects consumers, will work to keep Georgia growing, learning, and safe, and will ensure Georgia moves forward and greater opportunity reaches all corners.
q: From cutting taxes, creating good-paying jobs, strengthening our pro-business environment, supporting law enforcement, and expanding school choice, to cracking down on criminals and gangs, and standing up for our God-given rights, my priority has always been to put hardworking Georgians first.

In the 2025 legislative session, I successfully worked alongside Governor Brian Kemp to author and champion his top legislative priority that reins in lawsuit abuse, protects consumers, and stands with our small businesses and job creators against powerful special interests.

positions.stance: Sponsored and supported legislation that puts students first and ensures parents have a voice in education; passed legislation addressing chronic absenteeism in schools and giving students resources; believes classrooms should focus on educating students for rewarding careers, not indoctrination.
q: As a state senator, I am proud to have sponsored and supported legislation that puts our students first and ensures parents have a voice in their child’s education.

Just this past session, we were able to pass and receive Governor Kemp’s signature on legislation that addresses chronic absenteeism in our schools and gives every Georgia student the resources they need to succeed.

positions.stance: Will fight for Georgia’s farm families as Lt. Governor, supports helping farmers find new markets and support them during crises and supports making it easier to start, operate, and grow a family farm.
q: Our state’s number one industry is agriculture, and I will always fight for Georgia’s farm families as Lt. Governor.
Thousands of crops and products are grown or produced using our food and fiber, and our leaders must continue to help our farmers find new markets and support them when crisis strikes.

positions.stance: Will take on tough fights in the legislature even within own party, brings leadership focused on conservative results not rhetoric and will strengthen laws and allocate tax dollars wisely to keep families safe.
q: I haven’t shied away from the tough fights in the state legislature—even when it meant taking on some in my own party.
That’s the kind of leadership I will bring to Georgia as our next Lt. Governor—one focused on conservative results, not rhetoric.

positions.stance: Supports Georgia's efforts to protect communities, hold criminals accountable, and make streets safer.
q: Under Governor Kemp’s leadership, Georgia has taken huge strides in protecting our communities, holding criminals accountable, and making our streets safer.

positions.stance: Will fight to dismantle criminal street gangs and retain law enforcement officers.
q: We cannot grow complacent in our fight to dismantle criminal street gangs across our state, and we must also continue to ensure Georgia remains competitive in recruiting and retaining the best law enforcement officers.

positions.stance: Would end unnecessary corporate tax credits, use savings to reduce state income tax, eliminate income tax in Georgia, prioritize families and safety in budget, maintain per capita spending lower than before, and was appointed to chair committee to eliminate state income tax.
q: Instead of asking families to pay more elsewhere, we should end unnecessary corporate tax credits and use those savings to continue reducing, and ultimately eliminating, the state income tax.
“In the AFY23 budget, we prioritized families and safety while remembering that this is not our money, but the taxpayers’.”

positions.stance: Opposes taxpayer-funded giveaways for corporations and AI data centers, has to fight big business lobby as well as RINOs, opposes corporate welfare, supports federal regulators and Supreme Court rejecting denial of credit to disfavored industries, and would keep more money in Georgians’ pockets, fight for Georgia families, and grow from the ground up.
q: The largest corporations in the world don't need taxpayer-funded giveaways, especially when many Georgians oppose AI data centers that could increase their power bills.
I've been, and continue to be, opposed to corporate welfare.

positions.stance: Would fight illegal immigration, stop woke ideology, keep boys out of girls sports, authored a bill to force sanctuary cities to comply with state laws, deport the illegal aliens currently here, have a legal, effective system in place to handle real immigrants, and would hold sanctuary cities accountable to fight illegal immigration.
q: We can trust Blake Tillery to fight Illegal Immigration, to stop woke ideology being forced down our throats, and to keep boys out of girls sports.
Blake authored a bill to force sanctuary cities to comply with our laws.

positions.stance: Opposes debanking, saying no lawful business or individual should be denied access to an essential service based on ideology; says SB 341 protects Georgians from being denied financial services for constitutionally protected beliefs; supports defending freedom of thought and First Amendment rights.
q: I spent a lot of time fighting against debanking because no lawful business or individual should be denied access to an essential service based on ideology.

SB 341 – Freedom of Speech and Belief Act Known by many as the “Debanking Bill,” this legislation protects Georgians from being denied financial services simply for holding constitutionally protected beliefs.

positions.stance: They want to get rid of cash bail system to get criminals back on the street faster; would hold justice system officials accountable and demand results to protect families; illegal aliens are biggest drivers of crime, including drug cartels and human trafficking.
q: They even want to get rid of the cash bail system to get them back on the street faster!
He will hold those in charge of our justice system accountable and will demand results that protect our families.

positions.stance: Says Georgia taxpayers were funding gender-altering surgeries through the State Benefit Plan and in prisons, says Georgians should not be forced to pay for elective procedures they disagree with, opposes forcing Georgians to pay for elective procedures they disagree with, and authored legislation to prevent taxpayer funding for gender-transition procedures.
q: SB 39 – Ending Taxpayer-Funded Gender Surgeries It is hard to believe, but Georgia taxpayers were funding gender-altering surgeries—both through the State Benefit Plan and in our prison system.
Georgians should not be forced to pay for elective procedures they fundamentally disagree with.

positions.stance: Authored a bill to ensure GA officials uphold the law or face consequences, would continue the fight he began in the State Senate and would continue to define his work in the State Senate.
q: He authored a bill that will ensure GA officials uphold the law – or face consequences!
As Lieutenant Governor, I will continue the fight I began in the State Senate.

positions.stance: Opposes cultural shifts like boys in girls’ sports and Drag Queen Story Hour, authored bill to stop Georgia taxpayers funding gender-altering surgeries and opposes boys competing in girls’ sports and taxpayer-funded gender-altering surgeries.
q: The cultural shift over the past few decades has been stunning. From boys competing in girls’ sports, to Drag Queen Story Hour, to taxpayer-funded gender-altering surgeries — this is not the Georgia any of us want for our children.
He authored a bill (SB 39) to put a stop to Georgia taxpayers funding gender-altering surgeries — both through the State Benefit Plan and in our prison system.

positions.stance: Would be tough on criminals to fight crime and opposes drug cartels poisoning our country and fighting for territory.
q: To fight crime, we have to be tough on criminals.
The drug cartels poison our country and fight for territory killing anyone in their path.

positions.stance: Standing up for gun manufacturers that have been debanked.
q: Blake is standing up for gun manufacturers that have been debanked.

positions.stance: Addressed traffic congestion, cost-of-living increases, mental health issues, and affordability in budget.
q: “We heard and answered calls from Georgians concerning traffic congestion. We heard and answered calls from state retirees related to cost-of-living increases. We heard and answered calls from our law enforcement communities who have been overrun with issues related to mental health. And we answered

positions.stance: Budget includes funds for storm relief, growth, healthcare, and residency programs for aging population.

positions.stance: Will fight Obamacare expansion, free students from Common Core, and stop new water regulations; noted Senate Bill 186 had support from CTCA and Piedmont, which owns Coweta’s local hospital; supports easing regulation called Certificate of Need, or CON.
q: Matt will aggressively reassert state’s rights in Georgia by fighting the expansion of Obamacare, freeing students from Common Core, and stopping new water regulations imposed by an EPA that has run amok.
Brass noted Senate Bill 186 had support both from CTCA and Piedmont, which owns Coweta’s local hospital and had opposed some earlier proposed changes to the CON law.

positions.stance: Would cut taxes, reduce regulations, and push back against federal mandates like Obamacare; believes government should foster environment for businesses to flourish by cutting taxes and reducing regulations.
q: This means allowing our businesses and families to keep more of their hard-earned income by cutting taxes, reducing regulations that hinder job creation, and pushing back against job-killing federal mandates like Obamacare.

Matt understands that it is not the role of the government to create jobs; it is to foster an environment in which both new and existing companies can flourish. positions.stance: Will hold politicians accountable to balance the budget without one-time money and get Georgia back to prosperity; supports rein in spending to balance the budget.
q: Matt will hold politicians in Atlanta accountable to balancing the budget without relying on one-time pots of money and get Georgia back on a path to prosperity.
Rein in Spending to Balance the Budget

positions.stance: Says committed to sponsoring meaningful legislation for Georgia and her citizens; says works to challenge status quo in effective and responsible manner.
q: > During my short time in office, I have made a commitment to focus on sponsoring meaningful legislation for the betterment of Georgia and her citizens.

Fueled by passion for responsible government, I constantly work to challenge the status quo and I will continue to do so in an effective and responsible manner, yielding positive results for our district.

positions.stance: Will defend 2nd Amendment rights from anti-gun regulations and enhance those rights.
q: Not only will he defend our 2nd Amendment rights from anti-gun regulations, but he will work to enhance those rights.

positions.stance: Believes in sanctity of life and will work to end abortion.
q: As the father of two boys, Matt believes in the sanctity of life, and will always stand up for the unborn by working to end the moral scourge that is abortion.

positions.stance: Says knows first-hand the importance of a complete and accurate count of Georgia residents.
q: As Chairman of the Senate Reapportionment and Redistricting Committee, Brass said he knows first-hand the importance of a complete and accurate count of Georgia residents.

positions.stance: Said the law is not the first step to radically changing marijuana policy in Georgia.
q: Although no lawmakers spoke out against the new law, Lt. Gov. Geoff Duncan said that the law is not the first step to radially changing marijuana policy in Georgia.

positions.stance: Supports mandating a 'bell-to-bell' cell phone ban in high schools, says students should be learning not checking phones, believes long-term bans will help focus and improve learning outcomes, supports bell-to-bell ban to help students be more present in schools, voted against a request from the City Schools of Decatur Board of Education, supports taxpayer-funded early learning for disadvantaged children.
q: The bill mandates a “bell-to-bell” ban of cell phones in high schools.
Our kids should be learning in school, not constantly checking their phones for social media alerts or playing games.

positions.stance: Supports new voting machines near final approval after Senate passage; says cannot support measures directed to help Republican senators in re-election efforts; says Senator Dolezal’s attempt to court Trump’s endorsement went down in flames.
q: AJC: New Georgia voting machines near final approval after passing Senate
I obviously could not support these silly measures, which most seem directed to help certain Republican senators in their re-election efforts or statewide primary campaigns.

positions.stance: Supports legislation to check Georgia Power’s influence and limit data center utility price hikes; says consumer protections portion of the bill is not protective enough of billpayers; opposes SB 410 for lacking safeguards against consumer risks.
q: We discussed the pressing affordability crisis crushing Georgians’ pocket books and how Senate Democrats are fighting for legislation to check Georgia Power’s influence and make sure data centers don’t jack up utility prices for consumers.
The consumer protections portion of the bill is just the PSC rule and is not protective enough of billpayers.

positions.stance: HB 1001, the bill to lower the state income tax from 5.19% to 4.99%, passed both chambers; supports pushing date to eliminate codes to 2028; opposes eliminating state income tax and giving largest tax cut to ultra wealthy.
q: HB 1001, the bill to lower the state income tax from 5.19% to 4.99%, passed both chambers this week and is heading to the governor’s desk.
Therefore, the most prudent thing to do is to pass legislation that would push the date by which the codes must be eliminated to 2028.

positions.stance: Voted yes on bill to reduce restrictions on medical marijuana use, says legislature is tightening rules for medical marijuana companies, opposes President's policies that cut hospital funds and enable corruption, says health care is not a product that works in a free-market system and voted no on repealing CON but is still weighing the issue.
q: I was happy to vote yes on this bill and other states have already shown us the benefits of reducing the restrictions on the use of medical marijuana.
Meanwhile, the legislature is also tightening some of the rules that the medical marijuana companies must abide by to ensure the use is as intended.

positions.stance: Supports dedicated state funding for MARTA and transit, opposes Republicans' attempt to take over local transit systems, opposes Republicans' power grab to hinder public transit, and supports ending 'spring forward' and 'fall back'.
q: I believe it’s time to press state lawmakers on dedicated state funding for MARTA and transit.

The Republicans don’t support transit, and we aren’t even talking about pushing them to that – instead they are trying to take over the transit systems that localities have put in place despite the many hurdles the state has thrown at them, to ensure that there isn't more or more effective transit.

positions.stance: Supports referendum on controversial Early Childhood Learning Center, introduced SB 625 adopted by Senate and House, requested community referendum or legislation to stop the spiral over the ECLC and supports Girl Scouts of Georgia shaping the next generation of women leaders.
q: Crawford and Oliver to hold a referendum on their very controversial proposal for a new, very expensive Early Childhood Learning Center.
Community rancor is at a high, so a couple weeks ago, I introduced SB 625 and the bill was adopted by the Senate and today by the House.

positions.stance: Says banning Sharia Law is about preventing its incursion into American court system, says Senator Dolezal's bill intends to ban Sharia Law in Georgia and says bills like this were due to false rumors about President Obama being Muslim.
q: However, this is really about banning a supposed incursion of Sharia law into our American court system.
In a Facebook video posted on February 12th praising his bill, Senator Dolezal said the bill’s intent is to ban Sharia Law in the state of Georgia.

positions.stance: Supports worker-owned accounts for health insurance, paid leave, and retirement and supports support for public sector workers.
q: These accounts, owned by the workers themselves and administered by a bank or third-party provider, could be used to cover expenses such as health insurance premiums, paid leave, and retirement savings.
This is much needed support for our hard working public sector workers.

positions.stance: Served on State School Superintendent Schrenko’s Advisory Committee, says our children and adults must have access to quality education, says our state needs to reduce paperwork to allow teachers to teach, says money should be put back into the budget for schools, says will do what is best for our students and supports schools maintaining effective discipline for youth.
q: She was appointed by Congressman Nathan Deal to State School Superintendent Schrenko’s Advisory Committee and served on the team that revised the State’s Quality Core Curriculum.

We are all aware that our children and adults must have access to quality education if they are going to be able to master those skills and knowledge they need to compete and excel in our ever-changing world.

positions.stance: Has sponsored bills to improve agriculture in Georgia, says agriculture is important to the 11th district, supports our youth and all of agriculture, would defend ability to work the land and help feed community, and to defend agriculture you must understand the issues and challenges.
q: I have been an active member of the Agriculture and Consumer Affairs Committee since 2010 and have sponsored a number of bills to improve Agriculture in Georgia.
To defend Agriculture, you must understand the issues and challenges you face.

positions.stance: Opposes gun control laws, opposes red flag laws, received Defender of Freedom Award, says every 2nd Amendment bill has passed with support, supports ability to protect oneself and opposes efforts to infringe upon right to keep and bear arms.
q: Criminals will never abide by gun control laws, and armed, law-abiding Georgia citizens are no threat to public safety.
Red flag laws allow the Government to take your weapons upon the accusation of a crime. I fight these bills every day in the legislature because they rob your constitutional rights to Due Process.

positions.stance: Eliminated state income tax for most seniors, says a husband and wife can give up to $4,800 but must sign separate $2,400 checks, and would backfill gas tax cut next January to ensure road projects are not hurt.
q: Eliminated state income tax for most seniors
This means that a husband and wife can give up to $4,800; however, they must sign separate $2,400 checks to do so.

positions.stance: Opposes bills that rob constitutional rights to Due Process, would encourage public awareness that the best guarantee of liberty is a well-armed populace and says the 2nd Amendment guarantees citizens' ability to protect liberties and families.
q: I fight these bills every day in the legislature because they rob your constitutional rights to Due Process.
I will encourage the public’s awareness of the principle that the best guarantee of liberty is a well-armed populace of good citizens.

positions.stance: Would protect water use rights in Georgia, will protect water use rights in Georgia.
q: I understand this critical issue, and I will protect our water use rights in Georgia and have done so as a member of the House Agriculture Committee.
Water and agriculture go hand in hand. I understand this critical issue, and I will protect our water use rights in Georgia and have done so as a member of the House Agriculture Committee.

positions.stance: Says gas tax cut saves Georgians $200 million monthly and road projects would be hurt if not reimbursed, and says House Bill 1199 will temporarily suspend motor fuel tax for 60 days.
q: This gas tax cut saves Georgians about $200 million a month, and if we could not reimburse the gas tax void, that would stop quite a few road projects that all of us think are very important.
One bill we were excited to vote for this past week, and the Governor signed quickly, was House Bill 1199, which will temporarily suspend the motor fuel tax for 60 days.

positions.stance: Says corporations must use separate checks for contributions and state law requires disclosure of contributors, warns legislators may change bills to make them bad so must read and pay attention.
q:
A person who owns a corporation may give the maximum personally and the maximum from their business or corporation, but the contributions must be made with separate checks.

State law requires the disclosure of the name, address, occupation and employer of all individuals, businesses, or cor

Now is when you have to really be on your toes, as legislators start adding their bills to other bills, and other bills get changed just enough to make them bad, so you really must be reading the bills and pay attention.

positions.stance: Would give teachers a $3000 raise in 2019 and another $2000 in 2020.
q: Working with Governor Kemp for all of us to give teachers a $3000 raise in 2019 and will work again to make another $2000 in 2020.

positions.stance: Says policies support nine military installations and 130,000 jobs.
q: These policies to support nine military installations and their soldiers and their families, responsible for 130,000 jobs directly and indirectly.

positions.stance: Would create a study committee to examine PBM's impact on prescription costs and pharmacy access.
q: In other work during the week, we created a study committee to look at how pharmacy benefit managers ("PBM's") are manipulating consumer access and the cost of your prescription medications and also driving some pharmacies out of business.

positions.stance: Says must promote wellness incentives and increase educational options for doctors, nurses, and support staff; sponsored a bill that lowered allowable lead poisoning levels in children; organized a research and study committee to learn more about lead poisoning in children.
q: We must continue to promote wellness incentives, and increase educational options for additional doctors, nurses, and support staff.
During this past session, state Rep. Katie Dempsey, R-Rome, sponsored a bill that lowered the allowable lead poisoning levels in children from 20 deciliters to 3.5 deciliters.

positions.stance: Will focus on education, child advocacy, mental health, senior and veterans’ services, and workforce development, chaired House Study Committee on Postsecondary Education and Employment for individuals with disabilities and says bills will help support Georgia's families and safeguard children.
q: I will remain focused on education, child advocacy, mental health, senior and veterans’ services, as well as workforce development to support recruitment and retention in education, healthcare, and law enforcement.

HB 831 was a product of the House Study Committee on Postsecondary Education and Employment Options for Individuals with Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities, which Rep. Dempsey chaired in 2015.

positions.stance: Says Roe v Wade will be overturned, says supported the Heartbeat Bill and believes life begins at conception.
q: It appears that Roe v Wade will be overturned, throwing the abortion issue back to the states.
I am honored to have received the Georgia Life Alliance Certification and I was a proud supporter of the Heartbeat Bill.

positions.stance: Says Floyd County Police Department is here for senior citizens and will investigate crimes against them, believes it is vital to get message out to ensure each child's health and safety this summer.
q: The Floyd County Police Department is here for our senior citizens and is eager to investigate and help them resolve crimes that may occur against them.
I believe it is vital that we get this message out to the public to ensure each child’s health and safety this summer.”

positions.stance: Says froze state gas tax and cut income taxes for Georgians to alleviate inflation pressure; says top priority is to protect constituent dollars to ensure affordability.
q: I helped craft and support multiple measures this session to alleviate the pressure from Biden’s inflation by freezing the state gas tax and cutting income taxes for all hardworking Georgians.
My top priority is to protect the hard-earned dollars of every constituent to ensure that Georgia families can afford the necessities of life without sacrificing our future.

positions.stance: Says Gov. Deal signed bills championed by Rep. Dempsey into law; says provided background on Georgia’s work in data-informed policy space since 2017.
q: Gov. Deal Signs Bills Championed by Rep. Dempsey into Law

During her presentation, Rep. Dempsey provided background information about Georgia’s work in the data-informed policy space, which began in 2017 through the Joint Study Committee on Transparency & Open Access in Government.

positions.stance: Would prohibit disclosure of foster parents' personal information and would update child support laws to mirror federal changes.
q: HB 906, authored by Rep. Dempsey, will prohibit current and former foster parents’ personal information from being disclosed to the public.

SB 427, authored by State Senator John Kennedy (R-Macon) and sponsored by Rep. Dempsey in the House, will update Georgia’s child support laws to mirror federal regulatory changes that went into effect on Jan. 20, 2017.

positions.stance: Committed to overcoming barriers to access safe housing and increase employability.
q: I am committed to working to overcome barriers to access safe housing and increase employability.

positions.stance: Supports aging issues and has shown consistent support on concerns of Georgia's elderly.
q: The recipient of the award has also shown consistent support on aging issues, and has been willing to listen to the concerns of Georgia’s elderly.

positions.stance: Would expand employment options for Georgians with disabilities.
q: Also, I was extremely proud to continue my work in expanding employment options for Georgians with disabilities.

I will also fight to restore funding to pre-COVID-19 levels for our public schools so that Georgia students continue to receive a high-quality education and can compete for high paying jobs after graduation.

Recently, I helped pass legislation to ban surprise medical billing, cut prescription drug prices, and lower our maternal and infant mortality rates in Georgia.

positions.stance: Supports balanced transportation portfolio including road expansion, buses, shuttles, and transit trains; supports investing in future transportation technologies like autonomous vehicles and air taxis; supports a balanced transportation portfolio including traditional and new technologies.

I further believe that a true balanced transportation portfolio includes aggressive investment into the future including autonomous vehicles, air taxis and other new, upcoming technologies.

That’s why I’m co-sponsoring legislation to prevent Ai “deep fakes”.

Georgia's elections should be decided by Georgians.

positions.stance: Took a statewide leadership role in holding legislative hearings on securing Georgia’s election system; led a bipartisan effort to analyze new voting systems that leveraged cutting edge technology while giving Georgians the confidence of a physical paper ballot; sponsored a bipartisan bill that laid the groundwork for requiring a paper-verifiable statewide election system.

Through a rigorous 10-week committee process, Ed led a bipartisan effort to analyze new voting systems that leveraged cutting edge technology while giving Georgians the confidence of a physical paper ballot.

positions.stance: Supported House Bill 47 to reduce healthcare costs by allowing cross-state insurance purchases, opposed recreational marijuana legalization but supported Haleigh’s Hope Act for low-THC cannabis oil, supported Medicaid expansion with 20-hour work mandate, coordinated Senate Bill 36 for Prescription Drug Monitoring Program, expanded scope of practice for APRNs and PAs, and supported drug overdose reporters act.
q: Ed also supported House Bill 47 that reduced healthcare costs by allowing Georgians to purchase health insurance across state lines.

While opposed to the legalization of recreational marijuana, Ed supported Haleigh’s Hope Act, allowing Georgians to legally possess low-THC cannabis oil to address serious conditions such as uncurable seizures and nausea caused by intense chemotherapy.

positions.stance: Supported Senate Bill 33 requiring full bottom-up accounting of state spending, voted to cut own pay by 10% to safeguard teacher pay, supported constitutional spending limits and reduced state income tax, voted to cut legislative pay by 10% and eliminated the annual birthday tax on private automobiles.
q: Ed supported passage of Senate Bill 33, the Zero-based Budget Act, which requires state agencies every four years to produce a full, bottom-up accounting and justification of every dollar spent in every state program.
With COVID-19 devastating state tax revenues, Ed voted to cut his own pay by 10% to safeguard teacher pay and vital classroom resources.

positions.stance: Fully funded QBE formula, protected small class sizes, made teacher pay #1 in Southeast, provided school choice for special needs families; member of Senate Education Committee, active in Georgia education reforms; opposed changes to educational standards disrupting classroom learning.
q: With a laser focus on what’s best for kids, Ed has fully funded the QBE funding formula, protected smaller class sizes, made teacher pay in Georgia #1 in the Southeast, and played a key leadership role in providing school choice options for Georgia’s special needs families.
Ed is a member of the Senate Education Committee and has played an active role in many of Georgia’s most significant education reforms over the past decade.

positions.stance: Votes to eliminate state income tax on family income up to $100,000/year and end taxpayer subsidies to datacenters, fought against corporate cronyism shifting tax burden to working families, opposed tax breaks for data centers and their cost shifting to residential rate payers, supported tax incentive to reduce traffic congestion by promoting tele-working.
q: Senator Ed Setzler votes to eliminate state income tax on family income up to $100,000/year and end taxpayer subsidies to datacenters.
Ed has consistently fought against “corporate cronyism” that shifts the state’s tax burden to working families.

positions.stance: Supported bipartisan ethics reform House Bill 5, supported Senate Bill 300, helped define addictive design and supported property rights legislation in response to Kelo vs. New London decision.

positions.stance: Supported tax incentive to reduce traffic congestion and promote tele-working; prioritized state spending to fund traffic relief and gave local governments more options to fund traffic relief; cast deciding vote in passage of Senate Bill 200 creating statewide Planning Director to prioritize mobility projects.
q: Ed supported a thoughtful tax incentive to reduce traffic congestion and promote tele-working.

As a former member of the House of Representatives, Ed has provided leadership in prioritizing state spending to fund much needed traffic relief and giving local governments more options to fund traffic relief at the local level.

positions.stance: Fought to protect local ordinances encouraging smart sustainable growth and vulnerable water wildlife resources, championed protecting greenspace and low-density residential character of West Cobb, supported creation of a Statewide Water Management Plan.
q: Ed has been recognized by Georgia Conservation Voters for his successful fight to protect local ordinances that encourage the smart, sustainable growth of our communities and for being instrumental in the protection of vulnerable water and wildlife resources statewide.
Ed has been a champion of protecting greenspace and protecting the low-density residential character of West Cobb.

positions.stance: Led bipartisan effort to protect freedom of assembly and protest, provided law enforcement tools against domestic terrorism and is recognized statewide leader in protecting due process, personal privacy, free speech, self-defense, education and sanctity of human life.
q: Ed led a bipartisan, multi-racial effort to protect the freedom of assembly and protest in Georgia, receiving a bipartisan award from Asian Americans Advancing Justice in Atlanta while providing law enforcement the tools to crack down on true cases of domestic terrorism.
Ed led a bipartisan, multi-racial effort to protect the freedom of assembly and protest in Georgia, receiving an award from Asian Americans Advancing Justice in Atlanta.

positions.stance: Authored bipartisan bill to make AI systems subject to product liability standards and developed laws limiting abuse of cameras and drones by law enforcement, protecting children from harmful AI.

Ed has become a leader in the development of laws limiting the abuse of cameras and unmanned traffic control devices by law enforcement and in the protection of children from the potentially harmful effects of artificial intelligence (AI) in settings without adult supervision.

positions.stance: Has been active in criminal justice reform legislation for over a decade and worked to protect fundamental rights while providing law enforcement legitimate tools.

As the former Chairman of the General Law Subcommittee of House Judiciary Noncivil, Ed has worked tirelessly to protect the fundamental rights of Georgians while providing law enforcement officials with the legitimate tools they need to protect Georgia’s communities.

positions.stance: Supports effective law enforcement and protecting constitutional liberties, supported increased funding for public safety, crack down on gangs and sexual exploitation of children.

positions.stance: Runs to stop endless rate hikes, protect consumers, hold utility companies accountable, fight for affordable electric bills, demand greater transparency, ensure Georgia Power is held accountable, says data centers should pay their own way, must pay full cost of infrastructure, and demands transparency and accountability from PSC about data center costs.
q: She is running to stop endless rate hikes, protect consumers, and hold utility companies accountable.
I am running to fight for affordable electric bills, demand greater transparency, and ensure Georgia Power is held accountable for every dollar it asks customers to pay.

positions.stance: Would be critical third vote to restore accountability, says race will decide if PSC has majority willing to stand up to corporate power, demands transparency and accountability from Georgia Power, calls for holding Georgia Power accountable, says will fight for affordable electric bills and demand greater transparency, says Georgians should come before monopoly utility profits.
q: I am working hard to become the critical third vote that will restore accountability and put Georgia consumers first.
This race will decide whether Georgia finally has a Public Service Commission majority willing to stand up to corporate power, or whether unchecked rate hikes continue.

positions.stance: Calls to stop unnecessary rate hikes, says economic development should never come at expense of Georgia families, says will lower electric bills through greater accountability from Georgia Power, says data centers should pay their own way—not Georgia families, and says Georgia welcomes innovation but not at the expense of working families.
q: Stop unnecessary rate hikes.
Economic development should never come at the expense of Georgia families.

positions.stance: Says Georgia should require transparent impact assessments for data centers, says Georgians deserve truth about real cost of data centers, says need to understand impact of data centers on health and environment, says Georgia welcomes innovation but not at the expense of working families.
q: Before approving additional large-scale data centers, Georgia should require transparent, independent impact assessments that evaluate their effects on air quality, water resources, energy demand, public health, and the reliability of our electric grid.
Georgians deserve the truth about the real cost of data centers—not just in dollars, but in their impact on our health, our environment, and our communities.

positions.stance: Protects seniors, working families, veterans, and small businesses.
q: Protect seniors, working families, veterans, and small businesses.

positions.stance: Would make Georgia's public education system an envy of the nation; would invest in kids through smaller class sizes and offer a range of classes; would stop generational poverty by combining accountability, support for teachers and parents, to improve low performing schools.
q: We need to make Georgia’s public education system an envy of the nation.

Invest in our kids and our future, through smaller class sizes and offering every student the range of classes they need to grow and prosper, like art, music and theatre, languages, advanced placement and gifted, and career-technical classes.

positions.stance: Should reserve prison beds for the worst offenders, allow judges flexibility and discretion, reform minimum sentencing statutes, expand pre-trial intervention and drug courts, decriminalize marijuana, and allow law enforcement to focus on more serious crimes.
q: With the cost of housing an inmate in at over $20,000 a year, prison beds should be reserved for the worst offenders.
We should allow judges to do their job and give them the flexibility and discretion that they need to look at the facts of each individual case and issue appropriate punishment.

positions.stance: No child or parent should be worried about returning home after school; no child or parent should feel schools are becoming militarized; schools need to implement safety crisis plans to provide safe environments.
q: No child or parent should be worried about whether or not they will return home after school.
Also, no child or parent should feel that schools are becoming militarized.

positions.stance: Supports HB 204 Property Tax & Non-Tax Fees, which requires separating property tax billing from non-tax fees and prioritizing property tax payments, and voted yes on HB 661 Tax Liens.
q: HB 204 Property Tax & Non-Tax Fees (Rep. Smith voted Yes)

HB 204 (as passed by the House) will require local jurisdictions to separate property tax billing from non-tax fees/assessments (such as solid waste services) and to prioritize payment of property taxes.

positions.stance: Says low wages are troubling for families, promised to fight to strengthen the middle class and supports increasing child care reimbursement rates to be above market average.
q: Low wages are particularly troubling for families trying to raise children as research shows that a low family income decreases the chances of a child’s future success. 66% of Georgia voters agree that someone who works-full time should be paid enough to keep them out of poverty and voters in the co
When I was elected, I promised you that I would fight to strengthen the middle class, increase job opportunities, protect our communities, and seek solutions to the biggest problems facing our state.

positions.stance: Should invest in clean energy and new technologies to create jobs and help the economy and environment, should transition to solar, wind, hydroelectric, and other renewable energy sources, supports investing in clean energy and new technologies to create jobs and help the economy and environment.
q: We should invest in clean energy and new technologies that can create jobs and help our economy and our environment.
We should transition to solar, wind, hydroelectric, and other renewable sources of energy.

positions.stance: Voted for HB 429 to expand health coverage to people with pre-existing conditions and children with autism and would expand Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act to lower uninsured rates among Georgia's poor.
q: I am a compassionate advocate for you and I always cast my vote at the Capitol with you and your family in mind, that is why I voted for HB 429 to expand health coverage to people who have pre-existing conditions and children with autism.
One solution to the health care crisis would be for Georgia to expand Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act, which would lower the rate of uninsured among Georgia’s poor.

positions.stance: Has proposed legislation on voter registration and education, supports HB 819, which proposes provisions on elections, voter registration, and polling places.
q: During his service as State Representative, he has proposed legislation on voter registration and education.
On February 1, 2018, State Representative Michael Smith (D-Marietta) drafted a House Bill 819, proposing provisions on elections, voter registration, and polling places.

positions.stance: Can offer incentives to lower carbon emissions and supports policies to increase energy efficiency, encourage renewable fuels, and reduce pollution.
q: Companies, local governments, and individuals can be offered incentives to lower their carbon emissions.

Preserving our clean air, water, and natural environment is important for us and for future generations. With the growing threat of climate change, it is even more important to pursue policies that increase energy efficiency, encourage renewable fuels, and reduce pollution.

positions.stance: Announced Georgia State Senate passed House Bill 852 on March 19, 2018 and said proud to champion HB 852 and thanked Senate for approving it.
q: ATLANTA- State Representative Michael Smith (D-Marietta) today announced that the Georgia State Senate passed House Bill 852 on Monday, March 19, 2018, by a vote of 54-1.
"I was proud to champion HB 852, and I'd like to thank the Senate for overwhelmingly approving of this legislation," said Rep. Smith.

positions.stance: Voted Yes on HB 410 HOA Letter Fees.
q: HB 410 HOA Letter Fees: (Rep. Smith voted Yes)

positions.stance: Would eliminate the digital divide by providing broadband access to all communities.
q: Eliminate the digital divide by providing broadband access to all communities so our students can excel, and our small businesses can compete.

positions.stance: Supports public education and credits teachers for her path from poverty to college; fought to protect HOPE scholarship, expand technical colleges, fully fund K-12 schools; wants to use HOPE funds to expand Pre-K and childcare, especially for frontline workers.
q: A strong and consistent supporter of public education, Stacey credits her teachers for helping her find a path from poverty to college, law school and community service.

As a state legislator, she has fought to protect the HOPE scholarship’s original guarantee of an affordable education for all, led successful efforts to expand access to Georgia’s technical colleges and supported fully funding K-12 public schools.

positions.stance: Opposes Republicans blocking healthcare access and stripping equal protections under religious freedom legislation; won over $300 million for taxpayers in fight against Medicare fraud; will stand against Trump Administration's overreach on healthcare and local laws.
q: As a lawyer, a progressive and a person of faith, I can’t sit quietly as those same Republicans block access to health care for thousands of Georgians and try to strip away our fellow citizens' equal protections under the guise of so-called "religious freedom" legislation.
In one such case, she won more than $300 million for taxpayers as part of her ongoing fight against Medicare fraud.

positions.stance: Will stand against Trump-Kemp agenda and fight for shared values; would fight for a Commission that remembers its actual job: representing citizens; says duty is to people of District 57, not politicians in Washington, and will stand as firewall against Trump Administration's overreach.
q: As your State Representative, you can count on me to stand up to the Trump-Kemp agenda and put my experience to work to fight for the values we share.
I will fight for a Commission that remembers its actual job: representing the citizens of Georgia.

positions.stance: Will fight to establish easy ballot access, overturn voter ID laws, expand voting options; believes voter registration should be easy and permanent, voting at any precinct; says voting rights should be equal for all regardless of race, gender, or income.
q: Because voter suppression can happen both at the state and local level, as representative, I will continue my work to establish easy access to the ballot box and fight to overturn restrictive voter ID laws while expanding access to early and absentee voting.
I also believe that voter registration should be easy and permanent and that citizens should be able to vote at any precinct within their county lines.

positions.stance: Would identify and embrace environmentally conscious and family-friendly transit solutions; believes in supporting policies to keep air and water clean and address climate change; would fight to increase accountability for harmful chemicals and boost clean-energy jobs.
q: As Atlanta continues to grow, we must identify and embrace environmentally conscious and family-friendly transit solutions.

We have a moral and ethical responsibility to care for our planet. Doing that means supporting policies at the regional, state and national level that not only help keep our air and water clean, but also address the emergency created by climate change.

positions.stance: Strongly believes military grade assault weapons have no place on streets or in schools; would enact and enforce safeguards for gun owners including training, background checks and no violence history; says sensible gun laws are needed in the state.
q: I strongly believe that military grade assault weapons have no place on our streets and certainly not in our schools.
I will work to enact and enforce safeguards ensuring that every gun owner is properly trained, subject to background checks and has no history of violence.

positions.stance: Committed to economy where working in Georgia means affording to live in Georgia; would fight for a PSC that represents citizens, not corporations, and opposes rate hikes; called on Governor Kemp to cut prices for hardworking Georgians.
q: From cracking down on grocery price-gouging to incentivizing affordable housing, I am committed to an economy where, if you work in Georgia, you can afford to live in Georgia.

I didn't go to law school to watch powerful monopolies take advantage of working families. Right now, the PSC acts like a subsidiary of Georgia Power, rubber-stamping rate hikes that pad shareholder profits while your bill goes up. I will fight for a Commission that remembers its actual job: represe

positions.stance: Would fight for funding to expand mass transit systems and support investment in repairing infrastructure; believes in environmentally conscious and family-friendly transit solutions; would fight for funding to expand mass transit and repair infrastructure.
q: As your State Representative, I will fight for the funding needed to expand mass transit systems, including commuter rail, and I will support investment in repairing our infrastructure, including updating our roads and bridges.

As Atlanta continues to grow, we must identify and embrace environmentally conscious and family-friendly transit solutions. Too many people in our district either don’t have reliable transportation to get to and from work or school in a reasonable period of time, or sit for hours in traffic, missing

positions.stance: Organized Habitat for Humanity activities to expand housing access in Athens; would combat affordable housing shortage and fight against rising residential taxes.
q: While attending the University of Georgia, she tirelessly organized and coordinated Habitat for Humanity activities to expand housing access in the Athens area.

In the state legislature, I will put my experience to work to combat the shortage of affordable housing and fight against policies that lead residential taxes to sky rocket, while business property taxes hold flat.

positions.stance: Led efforts to protect civil rights, opposed abortion restrictions, supported criminal justice reform; sponsored anti-discrimination bills to guarantee all Georgians can live and work freely and equally.
q: During her twelve years as a state representative, Stacey led landmark efforts to protect the civil rights of all Georgians from discrimination allowed by so-called “Religious Freedom” legislation, strongly opposed attempts to further restrict safe, legal abortion access and reproductive health care
In the state legislature, I sponsored several anti-discrimination bills to guarantee that all Georgians can live and work freely and equally.

positions.stance: Will fight to increase minimum wage so no Georgians live in poverty; supports Georgia Earned Income Tax Credit, equal pay, affordable childcare.
q: In the state legislature, I will fight to increase the minimum wage, so that no hard working Georgians will live in poverty.
It’s also time we pass a Georgia Earned Income Tax Credit to put more money back in the hands of working people, while also ensuring equal pay and access to affordable childcare.

positions.stance: Says government needs to step back when it comes to reproductive rights; says passage of Heartbeat bill in 2019 convinced her to fight for rights of Georgia's women.
q: When it comes to reproductive rights, the government needs to step back.

positions.stance: Supports reducing tax burden on seniors, reducing state personal and corporate income tax rate, says Georgia achieved success through tax cuts and homeowner tax relief, proposed reducing state income tax rate, passed legislation that cut taxes and returned $1.1 billion to taxpayers.

HB 111 - Another historic tax cut that reduces the state personal and corporate income tax rate from 5.39% to 5.19%

positions.stance: Supports Georgia’s rural communities and forest landowners recovering from storms and natural disasters; focuses on policies that protect Georgia’s natural assets and promote responsible growth; supports conservation initiatives, environmental education, and legislation to sustain Georgia’s water, land, and energy resources.
q: This landmark legislation supports Georgia’s rural communities and forest landowners in recovering from storms and natural disasters.
As Chair of the House Natural Resources and Environment Committee, I continue to focus on policies that protect Georgia’s natural assets and promote responsible growth across the state.

positions.stance: Sponsored and secured $7 million for a charter school initiative, allocated $294 million to school safety, passed Georgia Promise Scholarship Act, established high demand career list and invested millions through Technical College System, and presented resolution declaring July 18, 2023, as Ayrshire Fiddle Orchestra Day.
q: I was honored to sponsor and help secure the $7 million Coweta County School Board budget request that funded the formation of CEC. This was a bold, community-wide charter school initiative—created in direct response to the workforce and employment needs voiced by local business and industry leaders
In response, Gov. Kemp touched on the $294 million that has been allocated to school safety thus far, and his budget proposal includes an additional $159 million to bolster those efforts.

positions.stance: Announced passing comprehensive tort reform legislation to limit civil lawsuits, expanded criminal offenses requiring bail, provided protections for property owners by ending squatters and penalizing false lease documentation, ensured sheriffs report illegal aliens in jails to ICE and passed resolution to support border security efforts, and supports combating human trafficking and child abuse through data sharing.
q: To combat this, he announced that one of his top priorities this session is passing comprehensive tort reform legislation designed to limit civil lawsuits.
Expanded the list of criminal offenses that require bail to make sure criminals show back up for court.

positions.stance: Made it easier to build drug recovery and rehab centers and expanded access to opioid antagonists, invested $150 million in mental health and supports authorizing child support and insurance policies for disabled children.
q: Made it easier to build drug recovery and rehab centers and expanded access to opioid antagonists - medications that block the effects of opioids in the system.

Invested over $150 million in Georgia Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Disabilities with a focus on mental health and passed legislation to protect mental health providers, allowing them to focus on their job instead of frivolous lawsuits.

positions.stance: Would remain the voice of the people of District 70 under the Gold Dome, would continue work representing District 70 through legislation and supports helping communities impacted by natural disasters.
q: My top priority remains being the voice of the people of District 70 under the Gold Dome.

positions.stance: Wrote law to fix delays in competency hearings, supported mental health reform, and opposed housing foster children in state offices; would work with partners to go after violent crime, criminal organizations, gangs, human trafficking, and illegal drug trade; supported stronger laws against deadly narcotics and human trafficking, fixed backlog in competency hearings.
q: He wrote the law that fixed long delays in competency hearings, has been a leading voice for mental health reform, worked to stop foster children from being housed in state offices, and supported stronger laws against gangs, dangerous counterfeit drugs, and human trafficking.
Brian will work with local, state, and federal partners to go after violent crime, criminal organizations, gangs, human trafficking, and the illegal drug trade.

positions.stance: Says children in state care were sleeping in government offices and hotel rooms with no bed, no school, and no one to count on, stands up for foster youth and vulnerable children, advances accountability standards for state programs, enforces Georgia’s laws firmly and impartially, and prioritizes protecting those in need through the law.
q: The clearest example of how Brian works is what he did for Georgia's foster children. For years, children in state care were sleeping in government offices and hotel rooms, not for a single night, but sometimes for weeks at a time, with no bed, no school, and no one to count on. Standing Up for Foster Youth & Vulnerable Children

positions.stance: Supports protecting Georgia's land, water, and farms; says Georgia's growth should not come at expense of clean water, healthy communities, or working farms; would protect Georgia's natural resources and shield family farms from unnecessary rules.
q: Protecting Georgia's Land, Water, and Farms
“ Georgia's growth should not come at the expense of clean water, healthy communities, or working farms. ”

positions.stance: Wants Georgia to be the best state for families with special needs and access to mental health care, carried Senior Care Home Reform through the Senate, supported comprehensive mental health access, cracking down on Medicaid fraud, and authored the Daniel D. Podsiadly Jr. Act.
q: Brian wants Georgia to be the best state in the country for families with special needs and for access to mental health care, and he believes the Attorney General should bring that same commitment to protecting consumers.
Senate RecordCarried Senior Care Home Reform (HB 987) through the Senate and supported the Opioid Settlement Fund distribution (SB 500).

positions.stance: Helped protect pay of law enforcement officers injured in line of duty; stood up for victims of human trafficking, backed opioid-settlement money for Georgia, and opposed Medicaid fraud; says every Georgian deserves to feel safe at home, at work, at school, and in their community.
q: He helped protect the pay of law enforcement officers injured in the line of duty, because an officer who was hurt while protecting the public should not face a financial crisis at home.

He stood up for victims of human trafficking, helped bring national opioid-settlement money home to Georgia communities, and backed strong action against Medicaid fraud so that money meant for people who need care is not stolen.

positions.stance: Wrote laws to protect seniors from abuse and improve nursing home care, says seniors who built the state should never live in fear of exploitation, protects Georgia seniors from abuse, scams, and neglect, authored Georgia’s Long-Term Care Background Check Program and the Grandparents Visitation Rights Act, and fights for our most vulnerable.
q: He wrote laws to protect seniors from abuse and to improve care in nursing homes.
As Attorney GeneralThe seniors who built our state should never live in fear of exploitation.

positions.stance: Would restore voter confidence, investigate voting irregularities, enforce election security standards, ensure every legal vote is protected and supported election integrity measures as Senate Judiciary Chairman.
q: Elections You Can Trust: Restoring Voter Confidence

As Attorney GeneralSecure, transparent elections are the absolute bedrock of a free republic. As Attorney General, Brian will investigate voting irregularities, enforce election security standards, and ensure every legal vote is protected so all Georgians have total confidence in election outcomes.

positions.stance: Helps create and fund the Georgia Farmland Conservation Fund to protect working farms that feed the state and carry its heritage forward.

Helped create and fund the Georgia Farmland Conservation Fund to protect the working farms that feed the state and carry its heritage forward.

positions.stance: Protected pregnant women in workplace, let workers use sick leave for family care, strengthened rights of grandparents raising grandchildren.
q: He protected pregnant women in the workplace, let workers use their sick leave to care for family members, and strengthened the rights of grandparents raising grandchildren.

positions.stance: Says growth should not come at expense of communities people call home.
q: Brian is proud that it remains one of the best states in the country to do business, but that growth should not come at the expense of the communities people call home.

positions.stance: Supports HB 888 to protect patients from unexpected medical bills by out-of-network doctors in emergencies; would reform senior care to better protect elderly individuals in personal care homes and assisted living facilities; supports updating laws for better oversight of facilities to protect vulnerable citizens.
q: House Bill 888 was sent to the governor, and it will protect patients from unexpected medical bills if they unknowingly receive treatment by out-of-network doctors in emergencies.
The House also passed vital legislation this week to reform senior care in Georgia to better protect elderly individuals living in personal care homes and assisted living facilities in our State.

positions.stance: Says voted yes on enhanced benefits for law enforcement without burdening taxpayers; says public safety is one of the governor’s priorities; says established Anti-Gang Task Force to fight gang activity.
q: I am very thankful for our hardworking law enforcement community, and I was proud to vote yes on these enhanced benefits for them, without putting a burden on taxpayers.
Another one of the governor’s priorities is public safety.

positions.stance: Says state Constitution requires balanced budget, would look carefully at savings while providing quality services, says programs would be reduced, says state budget needs to be reasonable and thrifty, supports Governor’s effort to reduce spending, would support economic development through appropriations for growing transit systems.
q: Our state Constitution requires us to have a balanced budget, a practice our counterparts in Washington should look to adopt!
The Appropriations Committee will look carefully at how these savings can be achieved while continuing to provide quality services to the people who need them.

positions.stance: Would create legislative solutions to aid rural communities and improve health care access, supports analyzing and recommending policies to support freight and logistics industries, supports collecting taxable revenue from marketplace facilitators selling over $100,000 annually, and supports economic development across various industries through House funding.
q: While these departments find ways to save our tax dollars, the House will continue to lead the charge in creating legislative solutions that aid rural communities, improve the quality of life and ensure access to basic health care services for rural Georgians.
The commission was authorized to analyze and recommend comprehensive public policy that would support our freight and logistics industries, including our distribution centers in Walton County.

positions.stance: Would examine budget adjustments for agricultural education and research programs, says agriculture is the number one industry in Georgia, supports expanding funding for rural broadband and supporting agriculture industry, supports legislation allowing cultivation and processing of hemp and hemp products in Georgia.
q: We also spent time this week examining proposed budget adjustments for agricultural education and research programs that aid the state’s farmers and agricultural industry in a variety of ways.
Agriculture is the number one industry in Georgia, and we will remain committed to maintaining this title as we consider funding for these programs.

positions.stance: Supports a tribute in the State Capitol to educate citizens about the Holocaust, says will continue to dismantle Common Core curriculum and reduce required tests, says budget includes funding for largest salary increase in state’s history for teachers and certified personnel, would allocate $174,000 to hire school safety threat assessment trainers.
q: This tribute in the State Capitol will serve as an important reminder that we should never forget the events of the Holocaust, and it will educate Georgia citizens to help ensure that such atrocities are never committed again.
The governor stated that he will continue to dismantle ineffective Common Core curriculum and reduce the number of required tests that weigh down our education system.

positions.stance: Supports allowing virtual or electronic meetings during emergencies as authorized by the speaker, supports voting on more legislation on the House floor before the Cross Over deadline, says plans to increase adoption tax credit and lower adoption age, opposes legislation that mentions the name of the president.
q: House Resolution 1507 would amend the Rules for the House to allow for official virtual or electronic meetings during emergency circumstances as authorized by the speaker of the House.
With our “Cross Over” deadline approaching, we will continue to vote on even more legislation on the House floor.

positions.stance: Says enacted law imposes lifetime commercial driver’s license ban for human trafficking convictions, supports SB 158 authorizing DFCS to provide emergency care for child trafficking victims and supports expanding state’s accountability courts within Criminal Justice Coordinating Council.
q: When enacted into law, it imposes a lifetime commercial driver’s license ban in Georgia for those convicted of a human trafficking crime.

Another meaningful piece of legislation that passed in the House this week was SB 158, the “Anti-Human Trafficking Protective Response Act,” which authorizes the Division of Family and Children Services (DFCS) to provide emergency care and supervision for a child victim of human trafficking without

positions.stance: Says federal government awarded $34.6 million to modernize Port of Savannah loading docks, would allocate $2.48 million to establish initial budget for Atlanta-Region Transit Link Authority and supports Senate Bill 25 to clarify language allowing drivers to pass stopped school bus.
q: Additionally, the Georgia Ports Authority announced that the Port of Savannah has been awarded $34.6 million through the Port Infrastructure Development Grant by the U.S. Department of Transportation to modernize the port’s loading docks.

The innovative Atlanta-Region Transit Link (ATL) Authority is included in this appropriation and would receive $2.48 million to establish the initial budget to plan and govern transit projects in the 13-county Atlanta region.

positions.stance: Supports HB 64 to notify military installation’s family advocacy program of child abuse or neglect allegations and supports passing 23 military-friendly bills for service members and veterans.
q: HB 64 mirrors similar legislation that has passed in eight other states, and the bill calls for child welfare agencies, such as the Department of Family and Child Services, to notify a military installation’s family advocacy program when there are allegations of child abuse or neglect involving an a
Over the last two years, the House has supported Georgia’s brave military service members and our veterans by passing 23 military-friendly bills.

positions.stance: Says bill helps meet demand for reliable internet access.
q: This bill helps meet the growing demand for reliable internet access in Georgia.

positions.stance: Supports House Bill 849 to combat human trafficking in Georgia.
q: Our Senate counterparts passed House Bill 849, which is one of three legislative measures proposed by Gov. Kemp to combat human trafficking in Georgia.
