positions.stance: Would begin staffing and deployment audit to match assignments with public-safety demand; would increase visible patrol, improve deployment, reduce unnecessary bureaucracy, and allocate resources where calls for service and crime data show they are needed most; includes courtroom safety, prisoner movement, civil process, and threat assessment.
q: WHAT CHANGES ON DAY ONE Begin a staffing and deployment audit that compares every assignment to actual public-safety demand.
Increase visible patrol, improve deployment, reduce unnecessary bureaucracy, and put resources where calls for service and crime data show they are needed most.

positions.stance: Would expand supervisor and command leadership development; supports competitive compensation for people who serve Hall County; says powerful technology is a liability when policies, auditing, retention limits, access controls, and public accountability are weak.
q: Expand supervisor and command leadership development.
Support the people who serve Hall County: Competitive compensation.

positions.stance: Would fully oppose sanctuary policies preventing cooperation with federal authorities or law mandates; would cooperate with ICE if federal authorities determine an individual is unlawfully present; would operate a lawful jail, follow Georgia law, honor lawful detainers, protect constitutional rights, and cooperate with federal authorities.
q: THE PLAN My administration would fully oppose any sanctuary policies that prevent legally required cooperation with federal authorities or law mandates.
If federal authorities determine that an individual is unlawfully present and issue a lawful immigration detainer, the Sheriff’s Office will cooperate with ICE.

positions.stance: Says public safety must be properly funded, but taxpayers should not fund duplication, weak planning, automatic contract renewals, or programs that cannot demonstrate value; would begin a line-by-line operational spending and contract review with classifications: KEEP, IMPROVE, RENEGOTIATE, CONSOLIDATE, or ELIMINATE; says every tax dollar should have a job.
q: THE PROBLEM Public safety must be properly funded, but taxpayers should not be asked to fund duplication, weak planning, automatic contract renewals, or programs that cannot demonstrate value.
WHAT CHANGES ON DAY ONE Begin a line-by-line operational spending and contract review with KEEP, IMPROVE, RENEGOTIATE, CONSOLIDATE, or ELIMINATE classifications.

positions.stance: Would comply with Georgia immigration law and cooperate with federal authorities, focus on public safety, cooperate with ICE on detainers for violent crime, and make up to 300 jail beds available for ICE detainees if agreement meets standards.
q: I would comply with Georgia immigration law, including HB 1105 as amended, cooperate with federal immigration authorities, protect constitutional rights, and keep Hall County resources focused on public safety.

I would work with ICE and the appropriate Hall County officials to pursue an agreement to make up to 300 jail beds available for ICE detainees, provided the agreement meets applicable detention standards, protects necessary local jail capacity, and makes financial sense for Hall County taxpayers.

positions.stance: Supports safeguarding records for long-term protection and data restoration, would allow clerks to securely protect various types of records, supports program meeting needs of counties with varying IT support, supports protecting electronic records of 155 counties, supports restoring over 3.4 terabytes of data back to clerk servers and supports advising on records management and protection of historical records.
q: Safeguarding these records ensures their long-term protection and provides a reliable method for restoring lost data if necessary.
Enrollment in the program allows clerks to securely protect their real and personal property records, court data, accounting and business records, and general purpose documents, among others.

positions.stance: Supports second line of defense against data loss events or disasters.
q: The intent of the program is to serve as a second line of defense against a data loss event or larger disaster at the courthouse.

positions.stance: Supports operating without local, state or federal tax funds and under legislative oversight.
q: The Clerks’ Authority was created, implemented and continues to operate without receiving any funds through local, state or federal taxes, and its activities undergo constant legislative oversight.

positions.stance: Would have a sole commissioner as governing authority of Murray County, recognizes commissioner as official head of Murray County and would have commissioner control over county affairs as provided by law.
q: The commissioner shall be recognized as the official head of Murray County by state, federal, and other authorities for all purposes, including military and ceremonial functions.
The granting of a permit does not presume to give authority to violate or cancel the provisions of any other state or local laws regulating construction or the performance of construction.

positions.stance: Would allow officers to appoint, recommend personnel and compensation, and designate duties, while governing authority may fix employee compensation and remove employees at will.
q: The officers specified in this Act shall have the authority to appoint such deputies, clerks, assistants, and other personnel as they shall deem necessary to efficiently and effectively discharge the official duties of their respective offices.

Each of said officers shall, from time to time, recommend to the governing authority of Murray County the number of such personnel needed by his or her office, together with the suggested compensation to be paid each employee.

positions.stance: Would define annual salary as total compensation of clerk of superior court from public funds, including allowances and benefits, and similarly for sheriff and probate judge.
q: (b) Such annual salary shall be the total compensation of the clerk of the superior court from public funds, except that the clerk may receive in addition to such annual salary: (1) an allowance for his or her service in juvenile court as provided in Code Section 15-6-89; and (2) retirement, insuran

(b) Such annual salary shall be the total compensation of the sheriff from public funds, except that the sheriff may receive, in addition to such annual salary, retirement, insurance, social security, and other similar employment benefits to the extent otherwise authorized by law.

positions.stance: Considers paved and dirt roads critical infrastructure, would keep roadways cleaner by having individuals dispose of items, says culvert width limits road expansion capability, supports annexation up to last businesses on 247 Connector west of I-75, says needs deceleration lane and turn lane for Houser Mill Rd, says highly trafficked inner change is not kept up as it should.
q: Whether our paved or dirt roads, this is critical infrastructure and one of the county's largest investments as well as responsibility to protect and enhance to keep them from deteriorating or being blown out during a catastrophic storm.

This should help keep our roadways cleaner and save the county money because of many individuals bringing their items to a convenient location instead of the county having to pick up everything and it cluttering the ditch banks until it gets picked up.

positions.stance: Worked with Chief Doles to sell old fire station to fund a new fire station; notes that individuals with intense mental health issues need state care; believes public safety employees should not duplicate work.
q: Fire Station Norwood Springs Rd. worked with Chief Doles to sell the old fire station on Lakeview to put it back on the tax roll, help the neighborhood it was in look better, and help fund a much needed fire station on Norwood Springs Rd.

Ones with intense mental health issues are a much lower percentile of the overall population that has mental health illnesses, and these are the individuals that used to be in the protection and monitored care of state mental health institutions.

positions.stance: Discussed public private partnership to connect Ethan St/ Housers Mill Rd to Pilot; says Warner Robins, Byron, and Peach County work well together; says county will be a better place to live, work and do business.
q: Update: I have met with all property owners- and discussed conceptual layout with the city of Byron, and Warner Robins about a potential public private partnership to get this done. 2026 Update: we currently approved engineering for connecting Ethan St/ Housers Mill Rd to the Pilot (Goal) Picture of
Warner Robins, Byron, and Peach County are working together really well and this should go a long ways in getting things done.

positions.stance: Says with God's grace and hard work business was rebuilt, says easier access for local vendors would increase competition and local economy, says small vendors are disenfranchised and need change, would lower project costs through increased competition and faster service.
q: With God’s grace and a lot of hard work, I started back from scratch and slowly rebuilt the business.

Getting things easier so that more local vendors want to do business with their local governments would not only increase competition for these jobs and services, but it would also plow a lot of money back into the local economy.

positions.stance: Believes true health begins with spiritual and physical health, with God as the Author and Editor and says quality of life comes from putting God first.
q: I believe true health begins on the inside, with both spiritual and physical health and we do best when God is the Author and Editor of both!
I believe quality of life in family, friendships, work (and all other areas of life) comes by putting God first.

positions.stance: Supports 4% of 8% sales tax to help county without increasing property taxes and would roll back tax millage rate and add it back as fire and EMS tax.
q: The 4% of the 8% sales tax collection that comes back to Peach County is powerful in how it helps us to advance the county without putting additional tax burden on property owners (as well as lowering our property taxes through the LOST penny sales tax).

With the amount of work that is done together for medical emergencies, (in my opinion) it simply makes sense to consolidate fire and EMS. To support this, (Peach, Fort Valley and Byron) could roll back the amount needed in tax millage rate, and then add it back as a (fire and EMS tax).

positions.stance: Helped organize talks about regional sewer infrastructure planning.
q: Regional sewage plant and infrastructure planning: helped organize talks between the Development Authority of Peach County, City of Byron, City of Fort Valley, and the Fort Valley Utility Commission about regional sewer infrastructure planning.

positions.stance: Says seniors need a senior center for resources and activities.
q: This is something that was of concern from way back in though we had senior services in the south end of the county that would extend up into the north end of the county it simply was not the same in comparison to actually having a senior center that our seniors could go to for resources, activities

positions.stance: Would look for ways entities and local representatives can work together.
q: As commissioner At-Large, I will continue to look for ways all of our entities and local representatives can work together, (after all, the spokes in a tire perform much better when connected to the same hub).

positions.stance: Says expensive homes should help ISO rating for homeowners.
q: There are some very expensive homes out in this area, and it should really help the ISO rating for homeowners in this southeast area of the county.

q: Our Platform for A Better Georgia /.about-twoicons-title Our country was built on a promise: work hard, keep your nose to the grindstone, and your children will have a better life.
That promise is broken. /.about-twoicons-content

positions.stance: Builds vibrant communities with funded schools, affordable childcare, and affordable housing, and runs because of underfunded schools and a healthcare system leaving people behind.
q: Build vibrant communities. That means families who aren’t one illness away from bankruptcy, parents who can find affordable childcare, workers who can afford to live where they work, schools funded to succeed, and communities where our children can build a career without leaving home.

I'm running because the same failures I watched in Atlanta and saw across theUnited States are showing up here — in underfunded schools, in a healthcare system that leaves too many people behind, in a landscape that's being sold off piece by piece.I have seen this before. I know what causes it. And

positions.stance: States Georgia gives away $2.5 billion in tax revenues to data center companies and gets less than $400 million back.
q: This year alone, Georgia will give away $2.5 billion in tax revenues to data center companies and get less than $400 million back.

positions.stance: Protects environment, saying federal cuts to Forest Service threaten natural beauty and economy.
q: Protect our environment. Our lives are rooted in these ancient mountains. Federal cuts to the Forest Service — including the closure of our regional office and a budget slashed by two-thirds — threaten the natural beauty that defines our community and drives our economy.

positions.stance: Plans development thoughtfully, saying developers should pay full cost and requires campaign finance reform.
q: Plan development thoughtfully. Developers should pay the full cost of their projects instead of passing the bill to taxpayers. We need mixed-use development that holds its value — not strip malls and apartments that deteriorate and drive property values down. That requires campaign finance reform to

positions.stance: A fair shake includes clean air, seeing a doctor, affording to live where you work, and kids having something worth staying for.
q: A fair shake means breathing clean air, seeing a doctor when you’re sick, affording to live where you work, and knowing your kids will have something worth staying for. That’s livability. That’s what I’m running to rebuild.

positions.stance: Shares a plan for financial accountability in Woodbury, would apply financial responsibility experience as mayor, says financial accountability is critical to maintaining trust and preventing waste, reports regularly on budget in clear language, would treat every dollar as if it were their own and ensure transparent, accountable leadership, has built career on financial responsibility and will apply it as mayor.
q: My Plan for Financial Accountability in Woodbury

In my last post, I shared why the city’s budget matters to every single one of us. Today, I want to talk about how I’ve built my career on financial responsibility—and how I’ll apply that experience as mayor of Woodbury.

positions.stance: Committed to keeping dialogue open, clear communication, transparent hiring processes, and honest leadership, says transparent and accountable leadership is how he will lead and asks for vote for financial transparency.
q: I’m committed to keeping this dialogue open—listening, sharing updates, and working with you every step of the way.
Accountable and Transparent – A leader who is committed to clear communication, open reporting, and ensuring our department reflects the highest standards of integrity.

positions.stance: Supporting local businesses and exploring new opportunities for growth, supporting small businesses and local jobs, wants to grow Woodbury’s economic ecosystem by leveraging its history, culture, and potential, believes new investments should generate enough value to sustain themselves and the system.
q: Supporting local businesses and exploring new opportunities for growth
Supporting small businesses and local jobs

positions.stance: Would update water map to plan for upgrades before breakdowns, build a water infrastructure system we can count on, conduct regular evaluations of water pipes, tanks, and pumps, and commit to reliable water, clear communication, and trustworthy infrastructure.
q: Proactive Maintenance Instead of waiting for pipes to burst, we need to update our water map to get a clear picture of the condition of our system and plan for upgrades before breakdowns happen.
Moving Forward: Building a Water Infrastructure System We Can Count On

positions.stance: Would make parks a top priority and will organize a "Woodbury Parks & Gardens Committee" to refresh parks.
q: If elected mayor, I’ll make our parks a top priority — starting with small, visible steps that build real momentum.
One of my first initiatives will be to organize a “Woodbury Parks & Gardens Committee”, a city-led and community-powered group of volunteers to refresh our parks before the next season.

positions.stance: Says police department plays a vital role in protecting and building trust, would build a new direction for Woodbury’s police department.
q: In Woodbury, our police department plays a vital role in not only protecting us but also in building trust with our residents.
Building Trust and Safety: A New Direction for Woodbury’s Police Department

positions.stance: Would hire a new Chief of Police to manage operations and set department tone.
q: Our city needs to hire a new Chief of Police—someone who will not only manage day-to-day operations but also set the tone for what kind of department we want to have.

positions.stance: Water utilities, public works, and agencies must collaborate for efficient solutions.
q: Interdepartmental and Stakeholder Collaboration Water utilities, public works, city planning, finance, environmental agencies, and community groups all need to be at the table to ensure solutions are efficient and comprehensive—not piecemeal.

positions.stance: States city has lost millions in grants for roads, schools, and local services.
q: Over the past few years, our city has lost out on millions of dollars in grants, funding that could have supported our roads, schools, and local services.

q: The Proposed 2027 Budget shows a 9.35%, $488,715, increase in General Fund revenues compared to 2026.
Total proposed General Fund expenditures are $12,522,735, requiring a Combined Utilities Fund transfer of $6,806,788 to balance the budget.

positions.stance: Would introduce caustic earlier in treatment process to improve water quality, supports eliminating manganese through system-wide flushing and says previous testing of the proposed process produced favorable results.
q: Mr. Helms reported that since introducing caustic before filtration, the post-treatment manganese levels have decreased to .05, resulting in clear water leaving the plant.

As part of the City’s ongoing efforts to reduce manganese concentrations in the water system and improve overall water quality, the caustic feed is being rerouted to introduce earlier in the treatment process a chemical that makes it easier for the plant’s sand filters to remove manganese.

positions.stance: Would allow a dog grooming business on Monroe County Tax Parcel 041 015A.

At the congressional level, I was told that once the state backs an ARC grant application, it’s basically a done deal.

positions.stance: $5 million won’t cover the true cost of the proposed system; if the city implemented the proposed capital projects, it would require an additional 6-30% uniform rate increase to the recommended rate structure; eMI proposes a massive increase in water bills if the city adds a planned well and water tank.

“If the city were to implemented (sic) the proposed capital projects with the new well and tank this would require an additional 6-30% uniform rate increase to the recommended rate structure. … Comparatively, a uniform rate increase to the existing*rate structure would have to be increased as high a

positions.stance: Says the City didn’t authorize a needs assessment, cites grant application claims about eliminating private septic systems and wants to be assured the sewer project is necessary, not just economically feasible.
q: The City didn’t authorize a needs assessment, only an economic feasibility study of the proposed septic-to-sewer project.

More recently, City officials revised to 30,000–40,000 gallons “initially.”The grant application said the project will “eliminate the need for private septic systems … will be located throughout City limits.”

positions.stance: Local developers cited in the grant application were described as committed partners in Sky Valley’s economic development.
q: Local developers cited in the grant application, Mountain Modern LLC and Merrill Trust Group LLC, were described as committed partners in Sky Valley’s “economic development,” providing “letters of intent” promising a boutique hotel and 30,000 square feet of retail, and up to 60 jobs.

positions.stance: Will help write enabling legislation for eliminating Georgia’s income tax.
q: On September 17, 2025, Georgia Senate Appropriations Committee Chair Blake Tillery announced he has asked Benita to help write the enabling legislation for the Senate Special Committee on Eliminating Georgia’s Income Tax.

positions.stance: Asks developers to return to the drawing board and include the City and residents.
q: Developers must return to the drawing board and show good faith by including the City and residents.

KRIS BOWDEN.background: Won the race for Americus Councilmember District 3, Sumter County in 2025.

positions.stance: Says Authority cannot provide benefits to employees like the City and would address base pay for all city employees, starting with APD.
q: Americus City Council Member Kris Bowden noted that the Authority currently cannot provide benefits to employees like the City.

“If we’re going to attack the base pay of our APD, we also need to look at how we’re going to attack the base pay of all of our city employees.” Council Member Kris Bowden said the need was greatest at the Police Department.

positions.stance: Supports law-enforcement agencies working together with ICE.
q: “I support any and every one that is doing what is right and fair for all people.” When asked whether the APD should cooperate with ICE, Council Member Kris Bowden replied, “Yes, I believe all law-enforcement agencies should work together.”

positions.stance: Supports proposed improvements for Historic Pope Park including new pavilions and playground equipment; supports proposed Memorial Wall and new playground equipment at Pope Park; voted in favor of playground equipment proposal for T.C. Jeffords Park.
q: Staff also discussed proposed improvements for Historic Pope Park, including the installation of two new pavilions at a lower cost than the single pavilion currently in place, relocating and refurbishing the existing playground equipment from T.C. Jeffords Park for use at Pope Park, and the addition

The proposed Memorial Wall was also mentioned, along with Mayor Proctor’s recent meeting with a playground vendor, stating he was impressed with the proposal and requested that action be taken regarding new equipment.

positions.stance: Supports removal of overflowing dumpster at Johnson Street and Sadler Street, supports trimming limbs along Livingston Street, opposes RedSpeed cameras, says other ways should be used to fund police officers and supports establishing a uniform closing time of 2:00 a.m. for alcohol sales.
q: Councilman Isaac Jackson noted that the dumpster at the intersection of Johnson Street and Sadler Street is overflowing and should be removed if the associated project is complete.
Additionally, limbs along West side of Livingston Street need to be trimmed to prevent damage with school buses.

positions.stance: Would authorize mayor to execute resolution for equipment purchase; would schedule new dates for Fiscal Year 2026–2027 Budget Public Hearings; says the City's budget is in line with proposed figures and reduced by 2%.
q: Staff requested authorization for Mayor Proctor to execute the resolution for purchase, consistent with prior equipment financing approvals for the Sylvester Fire Department Aerial Truck.

C. 2026-2027 Fiscal Year Budget Mr. Chris Davis advised that, although Council previously planned to hold the first Fiscal Year 2026–2027 Budget Public Hearing during this meeting, new dates for all three required public hearings will need to be scheduled.

positions.stance: Voted to remove water/wastewater tap fee from council agenda, would not hold city responsible for tree debris removal by contractors, requested review of New Jerusalem Church property request and discussed property line concerns, approved exclusive ram sponsorship for the Worth Rams Touchdown Club.
q: Agenda At the request of Mayor Harold Proctor, Jr., removal of Item A: Water/Wastewater Tap Fee was proposed for the City Council meeting agenda.
Homeowners paying contractors to cut down trees and place them on the roadside to be picked up like storm debris and the city should not be responsible.

positions.stance: Voted in favor of Beer, Wine, and Alcoholic Beverage License renewals, supports Economic Development Authority and Worth County's contribution to projects, and voted to approve beer, wine, and spirits store application.
q: Upon motion by Councilman Giddens, seconded by Councilman Hamilton, the Council approved the three (3) proposed Beer, Wine, and Alcoholic Beverage License renewals.
The involvement of the Economic Development Authority and Worth County’s contribution was also mentioned, leading the City Manager and Finance Department to review current obligation.

positions.stance: Opposes program that emphasizes revenue over child protection in school zones, supports a proposed after-school initiative and supports academic support, enrichment activities, and a safe environment for students in grades 2–5.
q: He also expressed concerns that the program places too much emphasis on generating revenue rather than protecting children in school zones.

New Business A. Rams Learning Launchpad Afterschool Initiative Mrs. Sandra Anderson, Worth County native and educator at Worth County Elementary School, addressed Mayor and Council regarding a proposed after-school initiative, the Rams Learning Launchpad.

positions.stance: Would consider planning for lift station upgrades to accommodate future phases and trailers.
q: With additional units expected, he emphasized that planning and design for lift station upgrades should have been considered to accommodate additional phases and noted eighty (80) more trailers in the future.

positions.stance: Voted to approve animal control budget increase and MOU with humane society.
q: After further discussion, a motion was made by Councilman Giddens and seconded jointly by Councilmen Hamilton and Powell to approve the requested animal control budget increase and authorize execution of the proposed MOU with Best Friends Humane Society.

q: I voted NO because I believe this bill is a punitive attack on cities that uses homelessness as a political issue rather than addressing its root causes.
Instead of helping people get off the streets, it encourages lawsuits against local governments and pressures communities to criminalize poverty.

To be clear: I think local races should be non-partisan, and I suspect most of the hardest-right wing Republicans in the district do as well.

Tax bills like this require a 2/3 vote, but in general I don't see any reason to vote against another county adopting this change, provided local leadership is in favor.

I believe Georgians deserve policies that reduce homelessness, not simply policies that make homeless people less visible.

positions.stance: Would have voted No if large employers could be legally excused from requirements; believes Democratic Party is better for advancing policies that strengthen working families, protect democratic institutions, and preserve freedoms.

positions.stance: Would ensure every veteran has access to top-quality healthcare, reduce wait times, expand mental health services, improve coordination between VA facilities and community providers, and create a Caregivers Network as a one-stop resource for families.
q: I will fight to ensure every veteran has access to top-quality healthcare whether through a strengthened VA system or expanded access to trusted local providers so no one is left waiting or without care.
We must reduce wait times, expand mental health services, and hold the system accountable for real results.

positions.stance: Supports establishing reasonable term limits for members of Congress, supports a full ban on stock trading for elected officials and their families, and supports a full ban on stock trading for elected officials and their immediate families.
q: I support establishing reasonable term limits for members of Congress so no one can turn public office into a lifelong career.

Allowing members of Congress and their families to trade individual stocks while shaping policy betrays that vision and erodes public trust. That’s why I support a full ban on stock trading for elected officials and their immediate families because public office should be about service, not profit.

positions.stance: Opposes layers of unnecessary regulations favoring big corporations, supports investing in trade schools to strengthen workforce and economy, and would cut burdensome red tape, simplify compliance, and create a fair playing field for small businesses.
q: Small businesses are the backbone of our economy, but too many are being crushed under layers of unnecessary regulations that favor big corporations with teams of lawyers and lobbyists.

By investing in trade schools, we’re not just creating opportunities we’re strengthening our workforce, rebuilding our economy, and giving the next generation real, practical paths to success without crushing debt.

positions.stance: Would increase funding for trade and technical education and expand access, opposes underfunding of trade schools and pretense that four-year college is the only path to success.
q: I will fight to significantly increase funding for trade and technical education, expand access in our communities, and elevate these careers to the respect they deserve.

We have to stop pretending a four-year college is the only path to success. For too long, trade schools have been overlooked and underfunded, even as our country faces a critical shortage of skilled workers.

positions.stance: Will prioritize transparency, accountability, and community input, bring analytical security-focused energy to the Board, is committed to transparency in government, would advocate for open meetings and expanded communication, and supports proactive investment over reactive solutions.

ALISON COUCH.name: Alison Couch
ALISON COUCH.background: Ran as a Republican in the partisan races on record. In the November 3, 2026 general election (count not yet certified), led in the race for County Commission Chairperson, Columbia County.

positions.stance: Committed to pursuing property-tax relief for homeowners, managing growth to reduce burden, using growth to lower tax burden, focused on fiscal discipline and lower taxes, would reduce county government portion of property taxes.
q: I’m committed to pursuing meaningful property-tax relief for Columbia County homeowners.
By managing growth responsibly, expanding our tax base, and protecting taxpayer dollars, we can reduce the burden on families while maintaining the services our community relies on.

positions.stance: Would focus on maintaining public safety, affordability, neighborhoods and development with adequate infrastructure, continue investing in law enforcement, fire and emergency services as population grows, supports first responders and keeps communities safe as they grow, supports investments for first responders and public-safety professionals, supported leadership during the storm by listening, solving problems and working with responders.
q: Alison’s approach would focus on maintaining strong public safety, keeping the county affordable, protecting established neighborhoods and rural areas, and ensuring that development is supported by adequate roads, services and infrastructure.
Continue investing in law enforcement, fire and emergency services as the county’s population grows.

positions.stance: Has worked to protect taxpayers, strengthen public safety, improve infrastructure, ensure responsible growth, advocated for small businesses, brought fiscally responsible approach to county government, and would prioritize economic development that broadens tax base and creates quality jobs.
q: As a small-business owner, accountant, and current County Commissioner, I have worked to protect taxpayers, strengthen public safety, improve infrastructure, and ensure our growth is managed responsibly.

Alison’s advocacy for small businesses has taken her to Washington, where she has testified before the U.S. House Committee on Ways & Means, giving Georgia business owners a voice in national policy discussions.

positions.stance: Supports maintaining and expanding parks, recreation, public spaces and community amenities, modernizing older parks and planning new amenities for growing areas, a network of multi-use and golf-cart connections linking neighborhoods with parks and amenities, and investments in Parks & Recreation.
q: Maintain and expand the parks, recreation opportunities, public spaces and community amenities residents use every day.

Columbia County’s parks are an important part of its quality of life, and Alison’s priorities include continuing to modernize older facilities while planning new amenities for growing areas of the county.

positions.stance: Believed county needed to act before development occurred, supported White Oak Industrial Park while voting against proposals at Pumpkin Center and Byrd property, and believes county should take approach of setting high standards, protecting residents, and pursuing economic development with measurable community benefit.
q: As data-center developers began considering Columbia County, Alison believed the county needed to act before development occurred, rather than waiting for problems to arise.

Of three major data-center rezoning proposals considered by the Commission, Alison supported the White Oak Industrial Park location while voting against proposals at Pumpkin Center and the Byrd property.

positions.stance: Prioritizes preserving quality of life while addressing growth realities, supports maintaining desirable qualities and opposes proposals not judged based on their impact on residents.
q: As Commission Chair, Alison Couch’s stated priorities center on preserving Columbia County’s quality of life while addressing the realities that come with continued growth—from taxes and public safety to infrastructure, recreation and the appearance of the community.
Growth should not mean losing the qualities that made Columbia County a desirable place to live in the first place.

positions.stance: Supports White Oak data center for meeting strict standards and providing property-tax relief and says the project was paired with commitments to ensure energy infrastructure costs are borne by the end user rather than local ratepayers.
q: I supported the White Oak data center because it met strict standards and could provide meaningful property-tax relief.

The White Oak project was ultimately paired with commitments from Google and Georgia Power designed to ensure the project's energy infrastructure costs are borne by the end user rather than local ratepayers.

positions.stance: Provides oversight of county finances, operations and internal controls and supports good government that listens, spends responsibly and produces results.
q: As Chair of the Commission's Audit Committee and Management & Internal Services Committee, Alison provides direct oversight of county finances, operations and internal controls, helping ensure taxpayers' dollars are managed responsibly.
Her record reflects a simple belief: good government should listen carefully, spend responsibly and produce results that improve the everyday lives of the people it serves.

positions.stance: Supports growth accompanied by roads, water, sewer and public infrastructure and would explore transportation planning beyond adding more road lanes.
q: Her focus remains clear: growth must be accompanied by the roads, water, sewer and public infrastructure necessary to support it.
Transportation planning does not have to begin and end with adding more lanes to roads.

positions.stance: Would maintain community where families get value for taxes paid, including good roads and services.
q: Alison’s priorities would include maintaining a community where families receive meaningful value for the taxes and fees they pay, including good roads, quality parks, reliable public services, safe neighborhoods and amenities that improve everyday life.

positions.stance: Envisions a District 3 with exemplary safety, infrastructure, and public services, would ensure community receives necessary funding and attention for infrastructure needs, and would not back down until the work is done.

positions.stance: Would work with police and code enforcement to clean up properties and hold owners accountable, would develop programs that support youth and protect seniors, and would advocate for pay raises, community patrols, undercover operations, and video surveillance.

positions.stance: Would create environments to facilitate business growth and engage partners to invest, supports funding and strategic development projects to jumpstart revitalization and economic development.

positions.stance: Would focus on homeownership as a pathway to building wealth and would increase both rental and single-family housing options.

positions.stance: Would listen to neighbors and protect those seeking change, supports inclusivity and transparency in community engagement.

positions.stance: Supports establishing a Non-Emergent Transportation company to assist seniors and disabled neighbors.
q: Her commitment to community service expanded with the establishment of a Non-Emergent Transportation company aimed at assisting seniors and disabled neighbors in accessing necessary medical appointments, fostering a safe and healthy environment for them to thrive.

positions.stance: Would support necessary staffing to get the job done efficiently.
q: I will support the necessary staffing to get this job done efficiently.

positions.stance: Supports funding for programs like NSP and HOPE and partners with organizations for education.

positions.stance: Supports fostering a healthier, greener, and more connected community.
q: Jake's dedication to this cause reflects her commitment to the well-being of DeKalb County's residents, both young and old, fostering a healthier, greener, and more connected community.

positions.stance: Supports safer streets and stronger infrastructure, believes safe streets are the foundation of a thriving community, is committed to safety with improved lighting, crosswalks, and traffic calming measures, prioritizes public safety to create a secure environment for residents, and utilizes surveys to gather data on public safety and education to prioritize efforts.

LaTonya Wright believes that safe streets are the foundation of a thriving community.

positions.stance: Believes community input is vital in shaping infrastructure projects, believes collaboration is key to achieving safer streets and stronger infrastructure, would partner with businesses for infrastructure projects benefiting the community, is committed to community engagement and sustainable development, and forms committees with community members to ensure projects reflect people's needs.

LaTonya Wright believes that collaboration is key to achieving safer streets and stronger infrastructure.

positions.stance: Would implement better traffic management systems and pedestrian-friendly designs, would expand public transportation to reduce traffic and promote eco-friendly travel, would increase bus routes to underserved areas for reliable transportation and prioritizes road maintenance and upgrades for safe and efficient travel.

positions.stance: Supports promoting walking and biking to reduce car reliance and lower emissions, is committed to promoting sustainable development practices, supports environmentally friendly construction and energy-efficient solutions, and is committed to promoting green initiatives like community gardens and recycling programs.

LaTonya Wright is committed to promoting sustainable development practices in South Fulton.

positions.stance: Supports after-school programs for tutoring, mentorship, and recreation, prioritizes education to empower the next generation with success tools, uses surveys and data analytics to understand community needs and prioritize projects, and says educational support initiatives led to scholarship recipients enrolling in college.

By prioritizing education, Wright aims to empower the next generation and ensure they have the tools to succeed.

positions.stance: Supports local businesses with resources and incentives to stimulate the economy, focused on creating job opportunities by attracting new businesses and supporting local entrepreneurs.

positions.stance: Would invest in modern utilities for clean water and reliable energy.

positions.stance: Would implement workforce development programs for high-demand jobs.
q: Workforce Development Programs: Implementing training and education programs to equip residents with the skills needed for high-demand jobs.

positions.stance: Believes an informed and involved community is essential for effective governance.
q: She believes that an informed and involved community is essential for effective governance.

STEVE GAILEY.background: Ran as a Republican in the partisan races on record. Lost the Republican primary for County Commission - District 3, Hall County in 2026.

positions.stance: Believes residents are frustrated with tax increases and SPLOST referendums; says constituents refuse to vote yes for tax increases or SPLOST referendums; believes county leadership has lost touch with taxpayers and government spending is growing.
q: According to Gailey, residents throughout District 3 are increasingly frustrated with continued tax increases and SPLOST referendums while many long-promised projects remain unfinished or nonexistent.
“I have been hearing from constituents all over District 3 who are refusing to continue to vote yes for any tax increases or SPLOST referendums,” Gailey said.

positions.stance: Believes county commissioners should advocate for community priorities and infrastructure needs, says will challenge commissioners to ensure taxpayer dollars are distributed fairly, says promises for District 3 amenities never came to fruition, says will fight for improvements commissioners can advocate for, questions whether current proposals serve North Hall residents.
q: Although Gailey acknowledges that athletic facilities at the high schools are technically under the Board of Education, he believes county commissioners should advocate strongly for community priorities and infrastructure needs.

Gailey says he will not hesitate to challenge sitting commissioners when necessary and will work to ensure taxpayer dollars are distributed fairly throughout Hall County — especially in North and East Hall communities that many residents feel have been overlooked.

positions.stance: Emphasizes responsible and controlled development, opposes high-density residential growth, believes county cannot sustain 3.5 to 4 homes per acre, supports maximum of two units per acre where sewer is available, and believes experience will bring smart and controlled growth.
q: His campaign has emphasized responsible and controlled development that protects the character of North and East Hall while ensuring roads, schools, and infrastructure can handle future growth.
A central theme of the interview was opposition to high-density residential growth.

positions.stance: Would hold sitting commissioners accountable and bring county back to citizens, pledges full transparency and no backroom deals, says will call out commissioners who override decisions and demand explanations, believes county government can be leaner.
q: “I will hold sitting commissioners accountable when needed, and we will bring this county back to the citizens where it belongs.”
He pledged full transparency—no backroom deals—and committed to working cooperatively with colleagues like David Gibbs while remaining a strong advocate for District 3.

positions.stance: Critics out-of-town interests for not building affordable housing.
q: Gailey criticized the shift from local developers to out-of-town interests who maximize profit without building truly affordable housing and having the areas best interests as a priority.

positions.stance: Highlights commitment to public safety, responsible growth, and protecting taxpayers.
q: Gailey also highlighted his continued commitment to public safety, responsible growth, and protecting taxpayers as key priorities in his campaign.

positions.stance: Says Hall County needs to invest in facilities for year-round recreation.
q: Gailey says Hall County also needs to invest in facilities that support year-round recreational opportunities for local residents.

positions.stance: Adopts short-term water management practices, supports funding and improving wastewater treatment and capacity, supports funding for Best Management Practices programs, requires local governments to identify and protect water supply watersheds, spells out criteria for protecting water supply watersheds and natural areas, and promotes and protects natural resources and recreation.
q: In addition, the Regional Water Plan has adopted several Short-Term Water Quantity and Water Quality Management Practices, which the local comprehensive plan should include in order to manage water resources in a sustainable manner through the planning period and beyond.
Support and fund current permitting and waste load allocation process to improve the treatment of wastewater and increase treatment capacity. b.

positions.stance: Sanitation ordinance became effective after taking office, appoints members to county authorities, would protect community resources through efficient land use, reflects best practices for land use decisions, supports board members reflecting young professionals' interests and supports intergovernmental coordination and collaboration.

positions.stance: Leverage Housing Authority and Neighborworks to increase housing stock, would increase attainable housing options and support policies for families, seniors, and workers, expedite permitting and encourage zoning flexibility for smaller lots and homes, consider implementing recommendations from the Columbus Regional Housing Study, and ensure every resident has access to a sidewalk/trail and a park within walking distance.

We will increase attainable housing options and support policies that keep District 7 accessible for families, seniors, and working residents.

positions.stance: Expand youth initiatives and early intervention programs to prevent crime, support practical safety improvements like lighting and blight removal, supports law enforcement successes and community-driven strategies to reduce crime, strengthen partnerships to address root causes and repeat problem areas, and build on law enforcement successes and support community-driven strategies to reduce crime.
q: Expand youth initiatives, mentorship, and early intervention programsthat prevent crime before it starts.
Support practical safety improvementssuch as lighting, crosswalks, and blight removal.

Our City Council will advocate for well-maintained parks, trails, and neighborhoods, and support projects that improve connectivity through sidewalks, trails, and streetscapes.

positions.stance: Prioritize job growth and industrial investment at Jim Blanchard Industrial Park and create stronger connections between business resources and South Columbus business owners.
q: Prioritize job growth and industrial investment by focusing on opportunities at Jim Blanchard Industrial Park.

Create stronger connections between existing business resources (Chamber of Commerce, StartUp Columbus, and UGA Small Business Development Center) and South Columbus business owners, making it easier to access capital, mentoring, and technical assistance.

positions.stance: Prioritize investments connecting neighborhoods to schools, jobs, and parks and leverage streetscape improvements to strengthen South Columbus as a community hub.
q: Prioritize investments that connect neighborhoods to schools, jobs, parks, and community destinations like the RiverWalk, Columbus Museum, and Fort Benning.

Leverage streetscape improvements on South Lumpkin and Buena Vista Roads, along with momentum around Synovus Park and the VECTR Center, to strengthen South Columbus and South Commons as hubs for jobs, investment, and community activity.

positions.stance: Would work respectfully with Councilors and City staff to deliver projects on time and within budget, and deliver results by working collaboratively with Columbus Consolidated Government.
q: Work respectfully and collaboratively with fellow Councilors and City staff to deliver projects on time and within budget.
Our City Council will deliver results by working collaboratively with the Columbus Consolidated Government and staying accessible, transparent, and responsive to District 7 residents.

positions.stance: Believes government should work for residents with transparency, fairness, and measurable results, says decisions should be transparent, measurable, and open to public scrutiny, supports clear accountability measures, says transparency and accountability are essential with open communication and honest performance measurement, says government should serve residents, not burden them unnecessarily, and says promises mean little without execution and follow-through.
q: I believe government should work for residents — not against them — and that transparency, fairness, and measurable results are not optional, but essential.
Accountability: Decisions should be transparent, measurable, and open to public scrutiny.

positions.stance: Would diversify economy, expand commercial tax base, attract quality jobs, fast-track permitting for job-creating businesses, form workforce partnerships with colleges and training providers, recruit high-wage industries and track jobs created and retained.
q: Rockdale County must diversify its economy, expand its commercial tax base, and attract quality jobs while supporting small businesses and entrepreneurs.
Fast-track permitting for job-creating businesses

positions.stance: Believes youth intervention programs need expansion, emergency services must evolve, says rapid population growth has strained public safety infrastructure and community trust, would expand youth prevention programs, conduct a comprehensive public safety audit, hire additional first responders proportional to population growth, and implement crisis response teams including mental health professionals.
q: Youth intervention programs need expansion, and emergency services must evolve to meet modern demands.
Expand youth prevention, mentorship, and intervention programs

positions.stance: Believes county needs leadership ready to serve, respects homeowners and protects property rights, supports expanding town halls and public engagement, and supports a framework to protect property rights, reform code enforcement, and ensure fair treatment of homeowners.
q: It needs leadership ready to serve from day one—leadership capable of managing growth responsibly while protecting homeowners, strengthening public safety, supporting local businesses, and ensuring county government works efficiently for the people it serves.
Respect homeowners and protect property rights

positions.stance: Would expand recycling education and access, establish an Environmental Advisory Committee, protect green spaces and sensitive environmental areas and expand water conservation and stormwater management programs.
q: Expand recycling education and access
Establish an Environmental Advisory Committee

positions.stance: Says youth and seniors need expanded programming, access to services and safe spaces to thrive, would increase senior transportation and support services and would enhance aging-in-place and caregiver support programs.

Increase senior transportation and support services

positions.stance: Would expand broadband access countywide and would launch a broadband expansion feasibility study.

Launch a broadband expansion feasibility study

positions.stance: Would expand after-school and youth mentorship programs and would complete a countywide infrastructure assessment.
q: Expand after-school and youth mentorship programs

positions.stance: Supports creating an information clearinghouse for mental health resources, says will work to gather best practices in community partnerships for mental health, examines health and human service delivery and financing issues, includes indigent health care, mental health, and housing issues, would lead Health and Human Services Policy Committee.
q: Established by current ACCG President and Baldwin County Commissioner Henry Craig, the Committee is tasked with creating an information clearinghouse for all 159 Georgia counties to equip them with resources to address the complex mental health issue.

“It is such a privilege to serve on the ACCG Mental Health Committee, and to serve as a co-chair of the subcommittee, Community Partnerships,” says Commissioner Williams, “Commissioner Chris Gaines of Dawson County and I will work diligently to gather and record best practices in community partnersh

positions.stance: Would help counties identify resources and create partnerships, uses consensus-based process for discussing policy changes, develops positions on key issues for the Policy Agenda, and commits to smooth transition and community priorities.
q: Over the past several months, outgoing and incoming leaders have worked collaboratively to ensure a smooth and effective transition, underscoring their shared commitment to the community’s priorities and progress.
The work of the full Committee will also help counties identify critical local, state, and federal resources; establish effective initiatives; and create impactful partnerships.

positions.stance: Says litter-free environments attract businesses and protect wildlife, supports Keep Georgia Beautiful Foundation and its local affiliates.

positions.stance: Supports launching 'Operation Green Light' in support of local veterans and adopted a resolution supporting NACo initiative to honor veterans.
q: Rockdale County to Launch ‘Operation Green Light’ In Support of Local Veterans

Rockdale County adopted a resolution in support of the NACo initiative on October 11th, designating October through Veterans Day, November 11th, as a time to salute and honor our men and women who served in the Armed Forces.

positions.stance: Opposes county government banning lawful land use across entire county; believes data centers should be classified as new or heavy industrial with restrictions; believes future data center projects should be disclosed early for community input.
q: It doesn't give our county government the power to outright ban a lawful land use across the entire county.
Going forward, I believe data centers should either be classified in our zoning ordinances as a new classification altogether or as heavy industrial with additional restrictions.

positions.stance: Believes need to carefully consider tax abatement agreements, opposes subsidizing data centers with increased utility costs and supports spending tax dollars wisely with transparent and accountable financial decisions.
q: We also need to carefully consider any tax abatement agreements.
The citizens of Troup County should not be subsidizing large data centers by paying increased utility costs or taking on any kind of burden in order to land the deal.

positions.stance: Supports giving first responders the tools to serve and protect citizens and is committed to supporting first responders.
q: We need to give first responders the tools they need to serve our community and protect our citizens.
Committed to supporting first responders

positions.stance: Would not take position to ban all data centers.
q: It would be easy to simply take the position to "ban all data centers" and move on, but I don't make promises I know I can't keep.

positions.stance: Promises to be honest and transparent, listen to concerns, and ensure voices are heard.
q: If you elect me your next Troup County Commission Chairman, I promise to always be honest and transparent with you, and to listen to your concerns and make sure your voices are heard.

positions.stance: Supports investing in and maintaining key infrastructure.
q: Infrastructure – We need to continue to invest in and maintain our key infrastructure.

MARCUS VEAZEY.background: Ran as a Republican in the partisan races on record. Won the race for County Commission - District 2, Walker County in 2026 (unopposed).

positions.stance: Would maintain, improve, and expand infrastructure, strengthen roads, protect taxpayers, and ensure transparent communication, fiscal accountability, and accessible information for residents.
q: My commitment is to ensure that Walker County’s infrastructure is properly maintained, strategically improved, and responsibly expanded to meet future growth.
Marcus Veazey is running for District 2 to strengthen roads, protect taxpayers, and keep residents informed about county decisions.

positions.stance: Would invest in infrastructure planned, measured, and fiscally sound to protect taxpayers, advocate for responsible spending and transparent financial reporting, and prioritize core services, evaluate programs for effectiveness, and ensure growth does not outpace financial stability.
q: Investment in infrastructure must be planned, measured, and fiscally sound—protecting taxpayers while strengthening our county’s future.
As Commissioner, I will advocate for responsible spending, transparent financial reporting, and policies that protect taxpayers from wasteful expenditures.

positions.stance: Would support Sheriff’s Office, first responders, and judicial system, ensure law enforcement and emergency services have necessary resources and infrastructure, and prioritize community partnerships, rehabilitation, and road/neighborhood safety.
q: With decades of experience in federal law enforcement and local judicial service, I understand the importance of supporting our Sheriff’s Office, first responders, and judicial system.
I will work to ensure law enforcement and emergency services have the resources, training, and infrastructure necessary to serve effectively.

positions.stance: Would lead with transparency, communicate clearly with citizens, and make decisions serving long-term interests, and would be available, visible, and accountable to citizens of District 2.
q: As Commissioner, I will lead with transparency, communicate clearly with citizens, and make decisions that serve the long-term interests of District 2 and all of Walker County.
I will be available, visible, and accountable to the citizens of District 2.

positions.stance: Would prioritize road maintenance, drainage, and public facilities safety.
q: This includes prioritizing road maintenance and repair, improving drainage and stormwater management, and ensuring public facilities are safe and functional.

positions.stance: Led investigations involving healthcare fraud, public corruption, and organized crime.
q: Throughout my FBI career, I led complex investigations involving healthcare fraud, public corruption, white-collar crime, organized crime, violent crime, international and domestic drug trafficking, and money laundering.

SARA FUCHS.name: Sara Fuchs
SARA FUCHS.background: Ran as a Democrat in the partisan races on record. In the November 3, 2026 general election (count not yet certified), trailed in the race for State House District 49. Other roles on record: PTA president at a Title 1 elementary school and now serve, Student Governance Council.

positions.stance: Notes Georgia's pre-K program no longer has room for every 4-year-old, leaving families to pay out of pocket; believes no child's education should depend on parents' ability to afford contributions; fights to fully fund K-12 public education so no classroom goes without.
q: Georgia's pre-K program, once a national model, no longer has room for every 4-year-old whose parents want a spot, leaving families to pay out of pocket for childcare they were promised would be free.
Sara Fuchs believes no child's education, from their first classroom to their diploma, should depend on how much their parents can afford to chip in.

positions.stance: Notes Georgia hasn't expanded Medicaid, leaving hundreds of thousands uninsured; supports expanding Medicaid to cover uninsured neighbors; supports lowering healthcare costs for working families.
q: The problem: Georgia is one of the last states in the country that still hasn't expanded Medicaid, leaving hundreds of thousands of Georgians without coverage.
Expand Medicaid and bring Georgia's own federal tax dollars home to cover hundreds of thousands of uninsured neighbors.

positions.stance: Supports targeted relief on everyday essentials, including easing local sales tax burden on groceries and household basics; supports responsible property tax relief that protects homeowners, especially seniors, from rising valuations; opposes tax cuts benefiting higher earners and corporations while cutting real services.
q: Support targeted relief on everyday essentials, including exploring ways to ease the local sales tax burden on groceries and household basics.
Support responsible property tax relief that protects homeowners, especially seniors, from being priced out by rising valuations.

positions.stance: Notes longtime residents and young families can't afford housing, renters have no protections; notes incumbent's housing platform focuses on property tax exemptions for existing homeowners; supports policies to protect renters and homeowners, including tenant protections and rent safeguards.
q: Longtime residents are being priced out of the neighborhoods they grew up in, young families can't find a starter home, and renters have no real protections against sudden rent hikes.
Incumbent Chuck Martin's own platform on housing, "Protecting Home Values," is entirely about property tax exemptions for existing homeowners.

positions.stance: Supports restoring and expanding voting access in Georgia; opposes further restrictions on absentee and early voting; supports modernizing voter registration and protecting access to secure drop boxes and polling locations.
q: Fight to restore and expand voting access in Georgia.
Oppose further restrictions on absentee and early voting.

positions.stance: Supports policies that ensure data center developers, not ratepayers, pay for power and infrastructure; supports commonsense guardrails on new data center development, including protections for local water supplies; supports Georgia attracting investment without asking working families to subsidize it through power bills.
q: Support policies that ensure data center developers, not everyday ratepayers, pay for the power and infrastructure their facilities require.
Support commonsense guardrails on new data center development, including protections for local water supplies and the communities that host them.

positions.stance: Would recuse from votes with personal financial interest and disclose more financial holdings; supports mandatory disclosure and recusal rules for legislators with financial stakes in voted industries; would push for legislation barring industry contributions within 90 days of a related vote.
q: I'll recuse myself from any vote where I hold a personal financial interest, I won't take industry contributions in the 90 days surrounding a vote that affects that industry, and I'll disclose more than the law requires — not less, at a time when the legislature just made it easier for officials to
I also support mandatory disclosure and recusal rules for legislators who hold personal financial stakes in industries that they vote on.

positions.stance: States Georgia regulators approved a $16.3 billion data center buildout; supports data centers covering infrastructure costs and stronger conflict-of-interest rules.
q: Georgia regulators just approved a $16.3 billion buildout to meet data center demand — a cost that could land on ratepayers at $50 billion or more over time.

I'll push for data centers to cover their own share of new infrastructure costs instead of passing them on to you, and I'll support stronger conflict-of-interest rules for legislators who hold personal financial stakes in industries they vote on.

positions.stance: Opposes expanding guns into schools and college campuses.
q: Oppose expanding guns into schools and college campuses.

positions.stance: Notes Georgia enforces one of the most restrictive abortion laws in the country.
q: Georgia now enforces one of the most restrictive abortion laws in the country, banning care as early as six weeks into a pregnancy, before many people know they're pregnant, with real consequences for patients and for doctors trying to provide standard medical care.

positions.stance: Supports policies that help wages keep pace with the cost of living in North Fulton.
q: Support policies that help wages keep pace with the actual cost of living in North Fulton.

positions.stance: Believes the best path forward is built with the community, not simply presented to it, built on conversation, not promises, and committed to listening closely, staying connected, and turning what he hears into practical action.
q: Built on conversation, not promises — we listen to our neighbors, build practical solutions over excuses, and unite District 151 through results, not division.

positions.stance: Running to represent Georgia House District 151, shaped by conversations across the district, says priorities are shaped by the people of District 151.

positions.stance: Listening to parents, teachers, and students to strengthen schools and believes people do their best when they know someone is willing to stand beside them.

positions.stance: Says it's their plan with seven practical priorities shaped by continuous conversations and continuous listening across District 151.
q: It's our plan.' Seven practical priorities shaped by continuous conversations across District 151.

positions.stance: Supports building pathways to opportunity by supporting local employers and working families, standing with the entrepreneurs and local businesses that anchor our communities.
q: Building pathways to opportunity by supporting local employers and working families.
Standing with the entrepreneurs and local businesses that anchor our communities.

positions.stance: Working alongside law enforcement and neighborhoods.
q: Relationships over division — working alongside law enforcement and neighborhoods.

positions.stance: Hearing directly from families about access, affordability, and community health.
q: Hearing directly from families about access, affordability, and community health.

positions.stance: Offers practical solutions for roads, water, and connectivity.
q: Practical solutions for the roads, water, and connectivity District 151 relies on.

positions.stance: Progress begins when we make room for honest conversation, shared priorities, and respect.
q: Progress begins when we make room for honest conversation, shared priorities, and respect for every person who calls this district home.
